god_1324.name: God
god_1324.description: (A.S. and Dutch God; Dan. Gud; Ger. Gott), the name of the Divine Being. It is the rendering (1) of the Hebrew ’El, from a word meaning to be strong; (2) of ’Eloah_, plural _’Elohim. The singular form, Eloah, is used only in poetry. The plural form is more commonly used in all parts of the Bible, The Hebrew word…

holy_spirit_7400.name: Holy Spirit
holy_spirit_7400.description:
The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

 His personality is proved (1) from the fact that the attributes of personality, as intelligence and volition, are ascribed to him (John 14:17, 26; 15:26; 1 Cor. 2:10, 11; 12:11). He reproves, helps, glorifies, intercedes (John 16:7-13; Rom. 8:26). (2) He executes the offices…

adam_78.name: Adam
adam_78.description: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Gen. 1:27-ch. 5). “God created man [Heb., Adam]…

eve_1231.name: Eve
eve_1231.description: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife (Gen. 3:20; 4:1). The account of her creation is given in Gen. 2:21, 22. The Creator, by declaring that it was not good for man to be alone, and by creating for him a suitable companion, gave sanction to monogamy. The commentator Matthew Henry says: “This companion was…

cain_533.name: Cain
cain_533.description: The first-born son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4). He became a tiller of the ground, as his brother Abel followed the pursuits of pastoral life. He was “a sullen, self-willed, haughty, vindictive man; wanting the religious element in his character, and defiant even in his attitude towards God.” It came to pass “in process…

abel_13.name: Abel
abel_13.description: (Heb. Hebhel), a breath, or vanity, the second son of Adam and Eve. He was put to death by his brother Cain (Gen. 4:1-16). Guided by the instruction of their father, the two brothers were trained in the duty of worshipping God. “And in process of time” (marg. “at the end of days”, i.e., on the Sabbath) each of them…

enoch_1191.name: Enoch (son of Cain)
enoch_1191.description: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.” This is the first “city” mentioned in Scripture.

irad_611.name: Irad
irad_611.description: Runner; wild ass, one of the antediluvian patriarchs, the father of Mehujael (Gen. 4:18), and grandson of Cain.

mehujael_1983.name: Mehujael
mehujael_1983.description: Smitten by God, the son of Irad, and father of Methusael (Gen. 4:18).

methusael_2041.name: Methusael
methusael_2041.description: Champion of El; man of God, a descendant of Cain (Gen. 4:18), so called, perhaps, to denote that even among the descendants of Cain God had not left himself without a witness.

lamech_1808.name: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
lamech_1808.description: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage (Gen. 4:18-24). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry. It has been called “Lamech’s sword-song.” He was “rude and ruffianly,” fearing neither God nor man.…

adah_69.name: Adah (wife of Lamech)
adah_69.description: The first of Lamech’s two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal (Gen. 4:19, 20, 23).

zillah_3080.name: Zillah
zillah_3080.description: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain (Gen. 4:19, 22).

jabal_673.name: Jabal
jabal_673.description: A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.

jubal_1748.name: Jubal
jubal_1748.description: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain. He was the inventor of “the harp” (Heb. kinnor, properly “lyre”) and “the organ” (Heb. ‘ugab, properly “mouth-organ” or Pan’s pipe), Gen. 4:21.

tubal-cain_2884.name: Tubal-cain
tubal-cain_2884.description: The son of Lamech and Zillah, “an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron” (Gen. 4:22; R.V., “the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron”).

naamah_2118.name: Naamah (line of Cain)
naamah_2118.description: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah (Gen. 4: 22).

seth_2504.name: Seth
seth_2504.description: Appointed; a substitute, the third son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4:25; 5:3). His mother gave him this name, “for God,” said she, “hath appointed me [i.e., compensated me with] another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.”

enos_1193.name: Enos
enos_1193.description: Man the son of Seth, and grandson of Adam (Gen. 5:6-11; Luke 3:38). He lived nine hundred and five years. In his time “men began to call upon the name of the Lord” (Gen. 4:26), meaning either (1) then began men to call themselves by the name of the Lord (marg.) i.e., to distinguish themselves thereby from idolaters;…

cainan_534.name: Cainan (antediluvian patriarch)
cainan_534.description: The fourth antediluvian patriarch, the eldest son of Enos. He was 70 years old at the birth of his eldest son Mahalaleel, after which he lived 840 years (Gen. 5:9-14), and was 910 years old when he died. He is also called Kenan (1 Chr. 1:2).

mahalaleel_1885.name: Mahalaleel (line of Seth)
mahalaleel_1885.description: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth (Gen. 5:12-17); called Maleleel (Luke 3:37).

jared_730.name: Jared
jared_730.description: The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2.

enoch_1192.name: Enoch (father of Methuselah)
enoch_1192.description: The son of Jared, and father of Methuselah (Gen. 5:21; Luke 3:37). His father was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he was born. After the birth of Methuselah, Enoch “walked with God three hundred years” (Gen. 5:22-24), when he was translated without tasting death. His whole life on earth was three hundred and…

methuselah_2042.name: Methuselah
methuselah_2042.description: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah. He was the oldest man of whom we have any record, dying at the age of nine hundred and sixty-nine years, in the year of the Flood (Gen. 5:21-27; 1 Chr. 1:3).

lamech_1809.name: Lamech (father of Noah)
lamech_1809.description: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah. Noah was the oldest of his several sons (Gen. 5:25-31; Luke 3:36).

noah_2210.name: Noah
noah_2210.description: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second…

shem_2613.name: Shem
shem_2613.description: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version. Shem’s name is generally mentioned first in the list of…

ham_1359.name: Ham
ham_1359.description:
Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24). The curse pronounced by Noah against Ham, properly against Canaan his fourth son, was accomplished when the Jews subsequently exterminated the Canaanites.

 One of the most important facts…

japheth_726.name: Japheth
japheth_726.description: Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth (10:21; comp. 9:24). He and his wife were two of the eight…

canaan_914.name: Canaan
canaan_914.description: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians. He had eleven sons, who were the founders of as many tribes (10:15-18).

gomer_1328.name: Gomer (son of Japheth)
gomer_1328.description: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe. He is generally regarded as the ancestor of the Celtae and the Cimmerii, who in early times settled to the north of the Black Sea, and gave…

magog_1882.name: Magog
magog_1882.description: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth. They are described as skilled horsemen, and expert in the use of the bow. The Latin father Jerome says that this word denotes…

madai_1880.name: Madai
madai_1880.description: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

javan_744.name: Javan
javan_744.description: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Dan. 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zech. 9:13). This word was universally used by the nations of the East as the generic…

meshech_2012.name: Meshech
meshech_2012.description: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the founder of a tribe (1 Chr. 1:5; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2, 3). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas. In Ps. 120:5 the name occurs as simply a synonym for foreigners or barbarians.…

tiras_2864.name: Tiras
tiras_2864.description: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

ashkenaz_338.name: Ashkenaz
ashkenaz_338.description: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race. They are mentioned in connection with Minni and Ararat, and hence their original seat must have been in Armenia (Jer. 51:27), probably near the Black Sea, which, from their founder, was first called Axenus, and…

riphath_2443.name: Riphath
riphath_2443.description: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

togarmah_2875.name: Togarmah
togarmah_2875.description: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

elishah_1154.name: Elishah
elishah_1154.description: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis. This may be meant by “the isles of Elishah” (Ezek. 27:7).

tarshish_2828.name: Tarshish (son of Javan)
tarshish_2828.description: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

dodanim_1018.name: Dodanim
dodanim_1018.description: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim (q.v.). In 1 Chr. 1:7, they are called Rodanim. The LXX. and the Samaritan…

cush_962.name: Cush (son of Ham)
cush_962.description: A son, probably the eldest, of Ham, and the father of Nimrod (Gen. 10:8; 1 Chr. 1:10). From him the land of Cush seems to have derived its name. The question of the precise locality of the land of Cush has given rise to not a little controversy. The second river of Paradise surrounded the whole land of Cush (Gen.…

mizraim_2100.name: Mizraim
mizraim_2100.description: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt (q.v.), and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower. The modern Arabic name for Egypt is Muzr.

phut_2354.name: Phut
phut_2354.description: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

seba_2481.name: Seba
seba_2481.description: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

havilah_1461.name: Havilah (son of Cush)
havilah_1461.description: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

sabtah_2451.name: Sabtah
sabtah_2451.description: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

raamah_2380.name: Raamah
raamah_2380.description: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

sheba_2567.name: Sheba (son of Raamah)
sheba_2567.description: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

dedan_998.name: Dedan (son of Raamah)
dedan_998.description: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the north-west coast of the Persian Gulf.

nimrod_2206.name: Nimrod
nimrod_2206.description: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10). The “land of Nimrod” (Micah 5:6) is a designation of Assyria or of Shinar, which is a part of it.

asshur_349.name: Asshur
asshur_349.description: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek. 27:23, etc.). In Gen. 2:14 “Assyria” ought to…

ludim_1835.name: Ludim
ludim_1835.description: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11). They are associated (Jer. 46:9) with African nations as mercenaries of the king of Egypt.

anamim_253.name: Anamim
anamim_253.description: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

naphtuhim_2150.name: Naphtuhim
naphtuhim_2150.description: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan. This city was the royal residence, it is said, of Queen Candace (Acts 8:27). Here there are…

casluhim_923.name: Casluhim
casluhim_923.description: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12). Their original seat was probably somewhere in Lower Egypt, along the sea-coast to the south border of Palestine.

zidon_2738.name: Zidon
zidon_2738.description: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19). It was the first home of the Phoenicians on the coast of Palestine, and from its extensive commercial relations became a “great” city (Josh. 11:8;…

heth_1510.name: Heth
heth_1510.description: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7). The Hittites were a Hamitic race. They are called “the sons of Heth” (Gen. 23:3, 5, 7, 10, 16, 18, 20).

jebusite_748.name: Jebusite
jebusite_748.description: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.). At the time of the arrival of the Israelites in Palestine they were ruled by Adonizedek (Josh. 10:1, 23). They were defeated by Joshua, and their king was…

amorite_237.name: Amorite
amorite_237.description: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions. On the early Babylonian monuments all Syria, including Palestine, is known as “the land of the Amorites.” The southern slopes of the mountains of Judea…

girgasite_1322.name: Girgasite
girgasite_1322.description: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1). They were a branch of the great family of the Hivites. Of their geographical position nothing is certainly known.…

hivite_1534.name: Hivite
hivite_1534.description: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15). They were probably a branch of the Hittites. At the time of Jacob’s return to Canaan, Hamor the Hivite was the “prince of the land” (Gen.…

arkite_308.name: Arkite
arkite_308.description: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

sinite_2755.name: Sinite
sinite_2755.description: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

zemarite_3036.name: Zemarite
zemarite_3036.description: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range. In the Amarna tablets (B.C. 1400) Zemar, or Zumur, was one of the most important of the Phoenician cities, but it afterwards almost disappears from history.

eber_1030.name: Eber (Heber)
eber_1030.description: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24). In Luke 3:35 he is called Heber.

elam_1049.name: Elam (son of Shem)
elam_1049.description:
Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles. The name Elam is an Assyrian word meaning “high.”

 “The…

arphaxad_312.name: Arphaxad
arphaxad_312.description: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years (Gen. 11:10-13; 1 Chr. 1:17, 18; Luke 3:36). He dwelt in Mesopotamia, and became, according to the Jewish historian Josephus, the progenitor of the Chaldeans. The tendency is to recognize in the word the name of the country nearest the…

lud_1834.name: Lud
lud_1834.description: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

aram_285.name: Aram (son of Shem)
aram_285.description:
The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).

 The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine…

uz_2908.name: Uz (son of Aram)
uz_2908.description: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

hul_1566.name: Hul
hul_1566.description: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

mash_1944.name: Mash
mash_1944.description: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia. Some have supposed that they were the inhabitants of Mount Masius, the present Karja Baghlar, which forms part of the chain of Taurus.

salah_2455.name: Salah
salah_2455.description: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

peleg_2308.name: Peleg
peleg_2308.description: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel. But more probably the reference is to the dispersion of the two races which sprang from Eber, the one spreading towards Mesopotamia and Syria, and…

joktan_1686.name: Joktan
joktan_1686.description: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber (Gen. 10:25; 1 Chr. 1:19). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab. Kahtan) was the progenitor of all the purest tribes of Central and Southern Arabia.

almodad_191.name: Almodad
almodad_191.description: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

hazarmaveth_1465.name: Hazarmaveth
hazarmaveth_1465.description: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). It is probably the modern province of Hadramaut, situated on the Indian Ocean east of the modern Yemen.

hadoram_1345.name: Hadoram
hadoram_1345.description: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

uzal_2911.name: Uzal
uzal_2911.description: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

ebal_2227.name: Ebal (son of Joktan)
ebal_2227.description: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

abimael_39.name: Abimael
abimael_39.description: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

sheba_2568.name: Sheba (son of Joktan)
sheba_2568.description: Heb. id. A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28), probably the founder of the Sabeans.

ophir_2253.name: Ophir
ophir_2253.description: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

jobab_1640.name: Jobab (son of Joktan)
jobab_1640.description: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

serug_2503.name: Serug
serug_2503.description: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

nahor_2142.name: Nahor (father of Terah)
nahor_2142.description: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

terah_2841.name: Terah
terah_2841.description: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia. He had three sons, Haran, Nahor, and Abraham, and one daughter, Sarah. He settled in “Ur of the Chaldees,” where his son Haran died, leaving behind him his son Lot. Nahor…

abraham_58.name: Abraham
abraham_58.description: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea. He then, with his father and his family and household, quitted the city of Ur, in…

nahor_2143.name: Nahor (brother of Abraham)
nahor_2143.description: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham (Gen. 11:26, 27; Josh. 24:2, R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran (Gen. 11:27-32). A correspondence was maintained between the family of Abraham in Canaan and the…

haran_1407.name: Haran (brother of Abraham)
haran_1407.description: Heb. haran; i.e., “mountaineer.” The eldest son of Terah, brother of Abraham and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah. He died before his father (Gen. 11:27), in Ur of the Chaldees.

lot_1830.name: Lot
lot_1830.description: (Heb. goral, a “pebble”), a small stone used in casting lots (Num. 33:54; Jonah 1:7). The lot was always resorted to by the Hebrews with strictest reference to the interposition of God, and as a method of ascertaining the divine will (Prov. 16:33), and in serious cases of doubt (Esther 3:7). Thus the lot was used at…

sarah_2473.name: Sarah
sarah_2473.description: Princess, the wife and at the same time the half-sister of Abraham (Gen. 11:29; 20:12). This name was given to her at the time that it was announced to Abraham that she should be the mother of the promised child. Her story is from her marriage identified with that of the patriarch till the time of her death. Her…

iscah_618.name: Iscah
iscah_618.description: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

pharaoh_2328.name: Pharaoh (during Abraham's Journey)
pharaoh_2328.description: The Pharaoh who was on the throne when Abram went down into Egypt (Gen. 12:10-20) was probably one of the Hyksos, or “shepherd kings.” The Egyptians called the nomad tribes of Syria Shasu, “plunderers,” their king or chief Hyk, and hence the name of those invaders who conquered the native kings and established a…

pharaoh_2331.name: Pharaoh (of the Exodus)
pharaoh_2331.description: The Pharaoh of the Exodus was probably Menephtah I., the fourteenth and eldest surviving son of Rameses II. He resided at Zoan, where he had the various interviews with Moses and Aaron recorded in the book of Exodus. His mummy was not among those found at Deir el-Bahari. It is still a question, however, whether Seti…

amraphel_244.name: Amraphel
amraphel_244.description: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain (Gen. 14:1, 4). It is now found that Amraphel (or Ammirapaltu) is the Khammu-rabi whose name appears on recently-discovered monuments. After defeating Arioch (q.v.) he united…

arioch_303.name: Arioch (king of Ellasar)
arioch_303.description: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer (Gen. 14:1, 9). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa. This Elamite name meant “servant of the moon-god.” It was afterwards changed into Rimsin, “Have mercy, O moon-god.”

chedorlaomer_926.name: Chedorlaomer
chedorlaomer_926.description: (= Khudur-Lagamar of the inscriptions), king of Elam. Many centuries before the age of Abraham, Canaan and even the Sinaitic peninsula had been conquered by Babylonian kings, and in the time of Abraham himself Babylonia was ruled by a dynasty which claimed sovereignity over Syria and Palestine. The kings of the…

tidal_2854.name: Tidal
tidal_2854.description: (in the LXX. called “Thorgal”), styled the “king of nations” (Gen. 14:1-9). Mentioned as Tudkhula on Arioch’s brick (see facing page 139). Goyyim, translated “nations,” is the country called Gutium, east of Tigris and north of Elam.

bera_467.name: Bera
bera_467.description: Gift, or son of evil, king of Sodom at the time of the invasion of the four kings under Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2, 8, 17, 21).

birsha_513.name: Birsha
birsha_513.description: Son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah whom Abraham succoured in the invasion of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

shinab_2708.name: Shinab
shinab_2708.description: Cooling, the king of Adamah, in the valley of Siddim, who with his confederates was conquered by Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

shemeber_2648.name: Shemeber
shemeber_2648.description: Soaring on high, the king of Zeboiim, who joined with the other kings in casting off the yoke of Chedorlaomer. After having been reconquered by him, he was rescued by Abraham (Gen. 14:2).

mamre_1923.name: Mamre
mamre_1923.description: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

eshcol_1218.name: Eshcol
eshcol_1218.description: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

aner_266.name: Aner
aner_266.description: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

melchisedec_1991.name: Melchisedec
melchisedec_1991.description: King of righteousness, the king of Salem (q.v.). All we know of him is recorded in Gen. 14:18-20. He is subsequently mentioned only once in the Old Testament, in Ps. 110:4. The typical significance of his history is set forth in detail in the Epistle to the Hebrews, ch. 7. The apostle there points out the superiority…

eliezer_1113.name: Eliezer (Abraham's Steward)
eliezer_1113.description: “Of Damascus,” the “steward” (R.V., “possessor”) of Abraham’s house (Gen. 15:2, 3). It was probably he who headed the embassy sent by Abraham to the old home of his family in Padan-aram to seek a wife for his son Isaac. The account of this embassy is given at length in Gen. 24.

hagar_1348.name: Hagar
hagar_1348.description: Flight, or, according to others, stranger, an Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid (Gen. 16:1; 21:9, 10), whom she gave to Abraham (q.v.) as a secondary wife (16:2). When she was about to become a mother she fled from the cruelty of her mistress, intending apparently to return to her relatives in Egypt, through the desert of…

ishmael_630.name: Ishmael (Son of Hagar)
ishmael_630.description: Abraham’s eldest son, by Hagar the concubine (Gen. 16:15; 17:23). He was born at Mamre, when Abraham was eighty-six years of age, eleven years after his arrival in Canaan (16:3; 21:5). At the age of thirteen he was circumcised (17:25). He grew up a true child of the desert, wild and wayward. On the occasion of the…

isaac_616.name: Isaac
isaac_616.description:
The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3). He was circumcised when eight days old (4-7); and when he was probably two years old a great feast was held in connection with his being weaned.

 The next memorable event in his life is that connected with the command of…

moab_2103.name: Moab
moab_2103.description: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

ben-ammi_451.name: Ben-ammi
ben-ammi_451.description: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

abimelech_40.name: Abimelech (King of Gerar)
abimelech_40.description: A king of Gerar in the time of Isaac, probably the son of the preceeding (Gen. 26:1-22). Isaac sought refuge in his territory during a famine, and there he acted a part with reference to his wife Rebekah similar to that of his father Abraham with reference to Sarah. Abimelech rebuked him for the deception, which he…

phichol_2341.name: Phichol
phichol_2341.description: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar. He entered into an alliance with Abraham with reference to a certain well which, from this circumstance, was called Beersheba (q.v.), “the well of the oath” (Gen. 21:22, 32; 26:26).

buz_529.name: Buz
buz_529.description: The second son of Nahor and Milcah, and brother of Huz (Gen. 22:21). Elihu was one of his descendants (Job 32:2).

aram_286.name: Aram (son of Kemuel)
aram_286.description:
The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10).

 The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine…

hazo_1468.name: Hazo
hazo_1468.description: Vision, one of the sons of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

bethuel_487.name: Bethuel
bethuel_487.description: The son of Nahor by Milcah; nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah (Gen. 22:22, 23; 24:15, 24, 47). He appears in person only once (24:50).

rebekah_2401.name: Rebekah
rebekah_2401.description: A noose, the daughter of Bethuel, and the wife of Isaac (Gen. 22:23; 24:67). The circumstances under which Abraham’s “steward” found her at the “city of Nahor,” in Padan-aram, are narrated in Gen. 24-27. “She can hardly be regarded as an amiable woman. When we first see her she is ready to leave her father’s house for…

thahash_2845.name: Thahash
thahash_2845.description: A badger, a son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother (Gen. 22:24).

ephron_1208.name: Ephron
ephron_1208.description: The son of Zohar a Hittite, the owner of the field and cave of Machpelah (q.v.), which Abraham bought for 400 shekels of silver (Gen. 23:8-17; 25:9; 49:29, 30).

zohar_3101.name: Zohar
zohar_3101.description: The father of Ephron the Hittite (Gen. 23:8).

laban_1803.name: Laban
laban_1803.description: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24). Jacob, one of the sons of this marriage, fled to the house of Laban, whose daughters Leah and Rachel (ch. 29) he eventually married.

keturah_1782.name: Keturah
keturah_1782.description: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country. Her nationality is unknown. She is styled “Abraham’s concubine” (1 Chr. 1:32). Through the offshoots of the Keturah line Abraham became the “father of many…

zimran_3086.name: Zimran
zimran_3086.description: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

jokshan_1685.name: Jokshan
jokshan_1685.description: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

medan_1978.name: Medan
medan_1978.description: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

midian_2075.name: Midian
midian_2075.description: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

ishbak_620.name: Ishbak
ishbak_620.description: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

shuah_2727.name: Shuah
shuah_2727.description: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

sheba_2569.name: Sheba
sheba_2569.description: Heb. id. A son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:3).

dedan_999.name: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
dedan_999.description: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

leummim_1819.name: Leummim
leummim_1819.description: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:3).

epher_1201.name: Epher
epher_1201.description: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

abida_21.name: Abida
abida_21.description: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

nebajoth_2164.name: Nebajoth
nebajoth_2164.description: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16). He had a sister, Mahalath, who was one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 28:9; 36:3).

kedar_1769.name: Kedar
kedar_1769.description:
Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13).

 It is the name for the nomadic tribes of Arabs, the Bedouins generally (Isa. 21:16; 42:11; 60:7; Jer. 2:10; Ezek. 27:21), who dwelt in the north-west of Arabia. They lived in black hair-tents (Cant. 1:5). To “dwell in the tents of Kedar” was to be cut off from…

adbeel_79.name: Adbeel
adbeel_79.description: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

mibsam_2046.name: Mibsam
mibsam_2046.description: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

mishma_2094.name: Mishma
mishma_2094.description: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

massa_1945.name: Massa
massa_1945.description: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

hadar_1341.name: Hadar
hadar_1341.description: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

jetur_911.name: Jetur
jetur_911.description: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

kedemah_1770.name: Kedemah
kedemah_1770.description: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

esau_1216.name: Esau (Edom)
esau_1216.description: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31). The circumstances connected with his birth foreshadowed the enmity which afterwards subsisted between the twin…

israel_682.name: Jacob (Israel)
israel_682.description: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old. Like his father, he was of a quiet and gentle disposition, and when…

aholibamah_1761.name: Aholibamah
aholibamah_1761.description: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 26:34), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

beeri_432.name: Beeri
beeri_432.description: The father of Judith, one of the wives of Esau (Gen. 26:34), the same as Adah (Gen. 36:2).

adah_414.name: Adah
adah_414.description: The first of Esau’s three wives, the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Gen. 36:2, 4), called also Bashemath (26:34).

elon_1182.name: Elon
elon_1182.description: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

bashemath_1887.name: Bashemath
bashemath_1887.description: The daughter of Ishmael, the last of Esau’s three wives (Gen. 36:3, 4, 13), from whose son Reuel four tribes of the Edomites sprung. She is also called Mahalath (Gen. 28:9). It is noticeable that Esau’s three wives receive different names in the genealogical table of the Edomites (Gen. 36) from those given to them in…

rachel_2386.name: Rachel
rachel_2386.description: Ewe, “the daughter”, “the somewhat petulant, peevish, and self-willed though beautiful younger daughter” of Laban, and one of Jacob’s wives (Gen. 29:6, 28). He served Laban fourteen years for her, so deep was Jacob’s affection for her. She was the mother of Joseph (Gen. 30:22-24). Afterwards, on Jacob’s departure from…

leah_1813.name: Leah
leah_1813.description: Weary, the eldest daughter of Laban, and sister of Rachel (Gen. 29:16). Jacob took her to wife through a deceit of her father (Gen. 29:23). She was “tender-eyed” (17). She bore to Jacob six sons (32-35), also one daughter, Dinah (30:21). She accompanied Jacob into Canaan, and died there before the time of the going…

zilpah_3081.name: Zilpah
zilpah_3081.description: Drooping, Leah’s handmaid, and the mother of Gad and Asher (Gen. 30:9-13).

bilhah_502.name: Bilhah
bilhah_502.description: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob (Gen. 29:29). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 30:3-8). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4). He was deprived of the birth-right, which was given to the sons of Joseph.

reuben_2429.name: Reuben
reuben_2429.description: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4). He showed kindness to Joseph, and was the means of saving his life when his other brothers would have put him to death (37:21, 22). It was he also…

simeon_2741.name: Simeon
simeon_2741.description: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26). He was detained by Joseph in Egypt as a hostage (42:24). His father, when dying, pronounced a malediction against him (49:5-7). The words in the Authorized Version…

levi_1820.name: Levi (patriarch)
levi_1820.description: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.” He is mentioned as taking a prominent part in avenging his sister Dinah (Gen. 34:25-31). He and his three sons went down with Jacob (46:11) into Egypt, where he…

judah_1751.name: Judah (patriarch)
judah_1751.description:
Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah. The name originated in Leah’s words of praise to the Lord on account of his birth: “Now will I praise [Heb. odeh] Jehovah, and she called his name Yehudah” (Gen. 29:35).

 It was Judah that interposed in behalf of Joseph, so that his life was spared (Gen. 37:26, 27). He took a…

dan_973.name: Dan
dan_973.description:
The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni). The blessing pronounced on him by his father was, “Dan shall judge his people” (49:16), probably in allusion to the judgeship of Samson, who was of the tribe of Dan.

 The tribe of Dan had their place in the…

naphtali_2149.name: Naphtali
naphtali_2149.description: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24). Little is known of him as an individual.

gad_1262.name: Gad
gad_1262.description:
Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18). In the Authorized Version of 30:11 the words, “A troop cometh: and she called,” etc., should rather be rendered, “In fortune [R.V., ‘Fortunate’]: and she called,” etc., or “Fortune cometh,” etc.

 The tribe of Gad…

asher_337.name: Asher
asher_337.description: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings. The place of this…

issachar_645.name: Issachar
issachar_645.description:
Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2). He had four sons at the going down into Egypt (46:13; Num. 26:23, 25).

 Issachar, Tribe of, during the journey through the wilderness,…

zebulun_3002.name: Zebulun
zebulun_3002.description: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history. He had three sons (46:14).

dinah_1012.name: Dinah
dinah_1012.description: Judged; vindicated, daughter of Jacob by Leah, and sister of Simeon and Levi (Gen. 30:21). She was seduced by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite chief, when Jacob’s camp was in the neighbourhood of Shechem. This led to the terrible revenge of Simeon and Levi in putting the Shechemites to death (Gen. 34). Jacob…

joseph_1710.name: Joseph (son of Jacob)
joseph_1710.description: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.” “The Lord shall add [Heb. yoseph] to me another son” (Gen. 30:24). He was a child of probably six years of age when his father returned from Haran to Canaan and took…

shechem_2588.name: Shechem
shechem_2588.description: The son of Hamor the Hivite (Gen. 33:19; 34).

hamor_1365.name: Hamor
hamor_1365.description: He-ass, a Hivite from whom Jacob purchased the plot of ground in which Joseph was afterwards buried (Gen. 33:19). He is called “Emmor” in Acts 7:16. His son Shechem founded the city of that name which Simeon and Levi destroyed because of his crime in the matter of Dinah, Jacob’s daughter (Gen. 34:20). Hamor and…

benjamin_463.name: Benjamin (patriarch)
benjamin_463.description: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place. His mother died in giving him birth, and with her last breath named him Ben-oni, son of my pain, a name which was changed by his father into Benjamin.…

eliphaz_1144.name: Eliphaz
eliphaz_1144.description: The son of Esau by his wife Adah, and father of several Edomitish tribes (Gen. 36:4, 10, 11, 16).

reuel_2430.name: Reuel
reuel_2430.description: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

jeush_913.name: Jeush
jeush_913.description: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

jaalam_662.name: Jaalam
jaalam_662.description: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

korah_1793.name: Korah
korah_1793.description: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

omar_2242.name: Omar
omar_2242.description: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

amalek_197.name: Amalek
amalek_197.description: Dweller in a valley, the son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau (Gen. 36:12; 1 Chr. 1:36); the chief of an Idumean tribe (Gen. 36:16). His mother was a Horite, a tribe whose territory the descendants of Esau had seized.

nahath_2146.name: Nahath
nahath_2146.description: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

seir_2485.name: Seir
seir_2485.description: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

lotan_1831.name: Lotan
lotan_1831.description: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

shobal_2719.name: Shobal
shobal_2719.description: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

ezer_1238.name: Ezer
ezer_1238.description: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

dishan_1015.name: Dishan
dishan_1015.description: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

lydia_1837.name: Lydia
lydia_1837.description: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13). She thus became the first in Europe who embraced Christianity. She was a person apparently of considerable wealth,…

ebal_1026.name: Ebal (son of Shobal)
ebal_1026.description: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

zavan_2944.name: Zavan
zavan_2944.description: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

akan_179.name: Akan
akan_179.description: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

uz_2909.name: Uz (son of Dishan)
uz_2909.description: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

aran_288.name: Aran
aran_288.description: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

bela_434.name: Bela
bela_434.description: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

beor_465.name: Beor
beor_465.description: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

hadad_1338.name: Hadad
hadad_1338.description: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

shaul_2477.name: Shaul
shaul_2477.description: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

baal-hanan_576.name: Baalhanan
baal-hanan_576.description: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

hadad_1342.name: Hadad
hadad_1342.description:
One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul. Called also Hadad (1 Chr. 1:50, 51).

 It is probable that in these cases Hadar may be an error simply of transcription for Hadad.

mehetabel_1980.name: Mehetabel
mehetabel_1980.description: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

mezahab_2043.name: Mezahab
mezahab_2043.description: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

jetheth_910.name: Jetheth
jetheth_910.description: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

elah_1043.name: Elah
elah_1043.description: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

mibzar_2048.name: Mibzar
mibzar_2048.description: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

iram_612.name: Iram
iram_612.description: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

potiphar_2368.name: Potiphar
potiphar_2368.description: Dedicated to Ra; i.e., to the sun-god, the Egyptian to whom the Ishmaelites sold Joseph (Gen. 39:1). He was “captain of the guard”, i.e., chief, probably, of the state police, who, while they formed part of the Egyptian army, were also largely employed in civil duties (37:36; marg., “chief of the executioners”).…

shuah_2728.name: Shuah
shuah_2728.description: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

onan_2250.name: Onan
onan_2250.description: Strong, the second son of Judah (Gen. 38:4-10; comp. Deut. 25:5; Matt. 22:24). He died before the going down of Jacob and his family into Egypt.

tamar_2821.name: Tamar
tamar_2821.description: The daughter-in-law of Judah, to whose eldest son, Er, she was married (Gen. 38:6). After her husband’s death, she was married to Onan, his brother (8), and on his death, Judah promised to her that his third son, Shelah, would become her husband. This promise was not fulfilled, and hence Tamar’s revenge and Judah’s…

pharez_2338.name: Pharez
pharez_2338.description: '=Pharez, (q.v.), breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3). Four hundred and sixty-eight of his “sons” came back from captivity with Zerubbabel, who himself was one of them (1 Chr. 9:4; Neh. 11:6).

zerah_2984.name: Zerah
zerah_2984.description: A son of Tamar (Gen. 38:30); called also Zara (Matt. 1:3).

pharaoh_2329.name: Pharaoh (of Joseph)
pharaoh_2329.description: The Pharaoh of Joseph’s days (Gen. 41) was probably Apopi, or Apopis, the last of the Hyksos kings. To the old native Egyptians, who were an African race, shepherds were “an abomination;” but to the Hyksos kings these Asiatic shepherds who now appeared with Jacob at their head were congenial, and being akin to their…

asenath_335.name: Asenath
asenath_335.description: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph (Gen. 41:45). She was the mother of Manasseh and Ephraim (50-52; 46:20).

manasseh_1928.name: Manasseh (son of Joseph)
manasseh_1928.description: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1). There is an account of his marriage to a Syrian (1 Chr. 7:14); and the only thing afterwards recorded of him is, that his grandchildren were “brought up upon Joseph’s knees” (Gen. 50:23; R.V., “born…

ephraim_1206.name: Ephraim
ephraim_1206.description: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20). The first incident recorded regarding him is his being placed, along with his brother Manasseh, before their grandfather, Jacob, that he might bless them (48:10; comp.…

pallu_2325.name: Pallu
pallu_2325.description: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9. He was the father of the Phalluites (Ex. 6:14; Num. 26:5, 8).

hezron_1519.name: Hezron
hezron_1519.description: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

carmi_920.name: Carmi
carmi_920.description: The last named of the four sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9).

jemuel_838.name: Jemuel
jemuel_838.description: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

ohad_2239.name: Ohad
ohad_2239.description: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

jachin_679.name: Jachin
jachin_679.description: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

zerah_3102.name: Zerah
zerah_3102.description: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

gershon_1305.name: Gershon
gershon_1305.description:
'=Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

 In the wilderness the sons of Gershon had charge of the fabrics of the tabernacle when it was moved from place to place, the curtains, veils, tent-hangings (Num. 3: 21-26). Thirteen Levitical cities fell to the lot of the Gershonites…

kohath_1790.name: Kohath
kohath_1790.description: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram (Gen. 46:11). He came down to Egypt with Jacob, and lived to the age of one hundred and thirty-three years (Ex. 6:18).

merari_2004.name: Merari
merari_2004.description: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16). He became the head of one of the great divisions of the Levites (Ex. 6:19).

hezron_1520.name: Hezron
hezron_1520.description: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

hamul_1367.name: Hamul
hamul_1367.description: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5). His descendants are called Hamulites (Num. 26:21).

jashub_1638.name: Jashub
jashub_1638.description: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

shimron_2706.name: Shimron
shimron_2706.description: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

sered_2501.name: Sered
sered_2501.description: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

elon_1183.name: Elon
elon_1183.description: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

ozni_1235.name: Ozni
ozni_1235.description: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

beriah_478.name: Beriah
beriah_478.description: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

serah_2492.name: Serah
serah_2492.description: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

heber_1469.name: Heber
heber_1469.description: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

bela_436.name: Bela
bela_436.description: The eldest son of Benjamin (Num. 26:38; “Belah,” Gen. 46:21).

gera_1298.name: Gera
gera_1298.description: The father of Ehud the judge (Judg. 3:15).

rapha_2447.name: Rapha
rapha_2447.description: A Benjamite, the son of Binea (1 Chr. 8:2, 37), a descendant of Saul.

huram_1569.name: Huram
huram_1569.description: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

jahzeel_706.name: Jahzeel
jahzeel_706.description: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

jesus_905.name: Jesus Christ
jesus_905.description: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah” (q.v.), the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament. It denotes that he was anointed or consecrated to his great redemptive work as Prophet, Priest, and King of his people. He is Jesus the Christ…

machir_1877.name: Machir
machir_1877.description: Manasseh’s oldest son (Josh. 17:1), or probably his only son (see 1 Chr. 7:14, 15; comp. Num. 26:29-33; Josh. 13:31). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead (Num. 26:29). They settled in land taken from the Amorites (Num. 32:39, 40; Deut. 3:15) by a special…

pharaoh_2330.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2330.description:
The “new king who knew not Joseph” (Ex. 1:8-22) has been generally supposed to have been Aahmes I., or Amosis, as he is called by Josephus. Recent discoveries, however, have led to the conclusion that Seti was the “new king.”

 For about seventy years the Hebrews in Egypt were under the powerful protection of Joseph.…

shiphrah_2710.name: Shiphrah
shiphrah_2710.description: Beauty, one of the Egyptian midwives (Ex. 1:15).

puah_2372.name: Puah
puah_2372.description: One of the two midwives who feared God, and refused to kill the Hebrew male children at their birth (Ex. 1:15-21).

daughter_of_pharaoh_988.name: Daughter of Pharaoh
daughter_of_pharaoh_988.description: The princess who adopted the infant Moses (q.v.), Ex. 2:10. She is twice mentioned in the New Testament (Acts 7:21: Heb. 11:24). It would seem that she was alive and in some position of influence about the court when Moses was compelled to flee from Egypt, and thus for forty years he had in some way been under her…

moses_2108.name: Moses
moses_2108.description: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt. This immigration took place probably about 350 years before the birth of Moses. Some centuries before Joseph, Egypt had been conquered by a pastoral Semitic race from Asia,…

jethro_2431.name: Jethro
jethro_2431.description: “The priest of Midian,” Moses’ father-in-law (Ex. 2:18)=Raguel (Num. 10:29). If he be identified with Jethro (q.v.), then this may be regarded as his proper name, and Jether or Jethro (i.e., “excellency”) as his official title.

zipporah_3095.name: Zipporah
zipporah_3095.description: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses (Ex. 2:21). In consequence of the event recorded in Ex. 4:24-26, she and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, when so far on the way with Moses toward Egypt, were sent back by him to her own kinsfolk, the Midianites, with whom they sojourned till Moses…

gershom_1302.name: Gershom
gershom_1302.description: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian (Ex. 2:22; 18:3). On his way to Egypt with his family, in obedience to the command of the Lord, Moses was attacked by a sudden and dangerous illness (4:24-26), which Zipporah his wife believed to have been sent because he had neglected to circumcise his son. She…

aaron_1.name: Aaron
aaron_1.description: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator. He was born in Egypt three years before his brother Moses, and a number of years after his sister Miriam (2:1, 4; 7:7). He married Elisheba, the daughter of…

laadan_1823.name: Laadan
laadan_1823.description: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi (Ex. 6:17; Num. 3:18, 21).

amram_242.name: Amram
amram_242.description: The son of Kohath, the son of Levi. He married Jochebed, “his father’s sister,” and was the father of Aaron, Miriam, and Moses (Ex. 6:18, 20; Num. 3:19). He died in Egypt at the age of 137 years (Ex. 6:20). His descendants were called Amramites (Num. 3:27; 1 Chr. 26:23).

izhar_658.name: Izhar
izhar_658.description: Oil, one of the sons of Kohath, and grandson of Levi (Ex. 6:18, 21; Num. 16:1).

hebron_1475.name: Hebron
hebron_1475.description: The third son of Kohath the Levite (Ex. 6:18; 1 Chr. 6:2, 18).

uzziel_2929.name: Uzziel
uzziel_2929.description: One of the sons of Kohath, and uncle of Aaron (Ex. 6:18; Lev. 10:4).

mushi_2116.name: Mushi
mushi_2116.description: Receding, the second of the two sons of Merari (Ex. 6:19; Num. 3:20). His sons were called Mushites (Num. 3:33; 26:58).

jochebed_1645.name: Jochebed
jochebed_1645.description: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59). She is spoken of as the sister of Kohath, Amram’s father (Ex. 6:20; comp. 16, 18; 2:1-10).

korah_1795.name: Korah (Levite)
korah_1795.description: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution. The old priesthood of the heads of families passed away. This gave rise to murmurings and discontent, while the…

mishael_2090.name: Mishael
mishael_2090.description: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

zithri_3096.name: Zithri
zithri_3096.description: The Lord protects, a Levite, son of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

elisheba_1162.name: Elisheba
elisheba_1162.description: God is her oath, the daughter of Amminadab and the wife of Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

amminadab_228.name: Amminadab
amminadab_228.description: The father of Nahshon, who was chief of the tribe of Judah (Num. 1:7; 2:3; 7:12, 17; 10:14). His daughter Elisheba was married to Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

nahshon_2144.name: Nahshon
nahshon_2144.description: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness (Ex. 6:23). His sister Elisheba was the wife of Aaron. He died in the wilderness (Num. 26:64, 65). His name occurs in the Greek form Naasson in the genealogy of Christ (Matt, 1:4; Luke…

nadab_2128.name: Nadab
nadab_2128.description: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah (Ex. 28:1). He afterwards perished with Abihu for the sin of offering strange fire on the altar of burnt-offering (Lev. 10:1, 2; Num. 3:4; 26:60).

abihu_33.name: Abihu
abihu_33.description: Father of Him; i.e., “worshipper of God”, the second of the sons of Aaron (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2; 26:60; 1 Chr. 6:3). Along with his three brothers he was consecrated to the priest’s office (Ex. 28:1). With his father and elder brother he accompanied the seventy elders part of the way up the mount with Moses (Ex. 24:1,…

eleazar_1062.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1062.description: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32). On Mount Hor he was clothed with the sacred vestments, which Moses took from off his brother Aaron and…

ithamar_649.name: Ithamar
ithamar_649.description: Palm isle, the fourth and youngest son of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:3). He was consecrated to the priesthood along with his brothers (Ex. 6:23); and after the death of Nadab and Abihu, he and Eleazar alone discharged the functions of that office (Lev. 10:6, 12; Num. 3:4). He and his family occupied the position of common priest…

elkanah_1167.name: Elkanah
elkanah_1167.description: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

ebiasaph_19.name: Ebiasaph
ebiasaph_19.description: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

phinehas_2349.name: Phinehas (Levite)
phinehas_2349.description: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished. For…

miriam_2087.name: Miriam
miriam_2087.description: The sister of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 2:4-10; 1 Chr. 6:3). Her name is prominent in the history of the Exodus. She is called “the prophetess” (Ex. 15:20). She took the lead in the song of triumph after the passage of the Red Sea. She died at Kadesh during the second encampment at that place, toward the close of the…

joshua_1727.name: Joshua
joshua_1727.description:
Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel. He is called Jehoshua in Num. 13:16 (A.V.), and Jesus in Acts 7:45 and Heb. 4:8 (R.V., Joshua).

 He was born in Egypt, and was probably of the age of Caleb, with whom he is generally…

hur_1571.name: Hur
hur_1571.description: The husband of Miriam, Moses’ sister (Ex. 17:10-12). He was associated with Aaron in charge of the people when Moses was absent on Sinai (Ex. 24:14). He was probably of the tribe of Judah, and grandfather of Bezaleel (Ex. 31:2; 35:30; 1 Chr. 2:19).

eliezer_1114.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1114.description: One of the two sons of Moses, born during his sojourn in Midian (Ex. 18:4; 1 Chr. 23:15, 17). He remained with his mother and brother Gershom with Jethro when Moses returned to Egypt. (Ex. 18:4). They were restored to Moses when Jethro heard of his departure out of Egypt.

bezaleel_490.name: Bezaleel
bezaleel_490.description: In the shadow of God; i.e., “under his protection”, the artificer who executed the work of art in connection with the tabernacle in the wilderness (Ex. 31:2; 35:30). He was engaged principally in works of metal, wood, and stone; while Aholiab, who was associated with him and subordinate to him, had the charge of the…

aholiab_170.name: Aholiab
aholiab_170.description: Tent of the father, an artist of the tribe of Dan, appointed to the work of preparing materials for the tabernacle (Ex. 31:6; 35:34; 36:1, 2; 38:23).

nun_2214.name: Nun
nun_2214.description: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

molech_2104.name: Molech
molech_2104.description: King, the name of the national god of the Ammonites, to whom children were sacrificed by fire. He was the consuming and destroying and also at the same time the purifying fire. In Amos 5:26, “your Moloch” of the Authorized Version is “your king” in the Revised Version (comp. Acts 7:43). Solomon (1 Kings 11:7) erected…

zurishaddai_3113.name: Zurishaddai
zurishaddai_3113.description: Rock of the Almighty, the father of Shelumiel, who was chief of the tribe of Simeon when Israel was encamped at Sinai (Num. 1:6; 2:12).

nethaneel_2188.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2188.description: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

eliab_1073.name: Eliab
eliab_1073.description: A son of Helon, and chief of the tribe of Zebulun at the time of the census in the wilderness (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

helon_1486.name: Helon
helon_1486.description: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

elishama_1155.name: Elishama
elishama_1155.description: A prince of Benjamin, grandfather of Joshua (Num. 1:10; 1 Chr. 7:26).

ammihud_223.name: Ammihud
ammihud_223.description: The father of the Ephraimite chief Elishama, at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53).

gamaliel_1276.name: Gamaliel
gamaliel_1276.description: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

pedahzur_2291.name: Pedahzur
pedahzur_2291.description: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

abidan_22.name: Abidan
abidan_22.description: Father of judgment; judge, head of the tribe of Benjamin at the Exodus (Num. 1:11; 2:22).

ammishaddai_230.name: Ammishaddai
ammishaddai_230.description: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:12; 2:25). This is one of the few names compounded with the name of God, Shaddai, “Almighty.”

pagiel_2264.name: Pagiel
pagiel_2264.description: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

ahira_157.name: Ahira
ahira_157.description: Brother of evil = unlucky, or my brother is friend, chief of the tribe of Naphtali at the Exodus (Num. 1:15; 2:29).

zuriel_3112.name: Zuriel
zuriel_3112.description: Rock of God, chief of the family of the Merarites (Num. 3:35) at the time of the Exodus.

hobab_1537.name: Hobab
hobab_1537.description: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro (q.v.), Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30. In Judg. 4:11, the word rendered “father-in-law” means properly any male relative by marriage (comp. Gen. 19:14, “son-in-law,” A.V.), and should be rendered “brother-in-law,” as in the R.V. His descendants followed…

eldad_1058.name: Eldad
eldad_1058.description: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people. He, with Medad, prophesied in the camp instead of going with the rest to the tabernacle, as Moses had commanded. This incident was announced to Moses by Joshua, who thought their conduct in this…

shammua_2545.name: Shammua
shammua_2545.description: One of the spies sent out by Moses to search the land (Num. 13:4). He represented the tribe of Reuben.

zaccur_2963.name: Zaccur
zaccur_2963.description: Father of Shammua, who was one of the spies sent out by Moses (Num. 13:4).

shaphat_2552.name: Shaphat
shaphat_2552.description: One of the spies. He represented the tribe of Simeon (Num. 13:5).

caleb_537.name: Caleb
caleb_537.description: The son of Jephunneh (Num. 13:6; 32:12; Josh. 14:6, 14). He was one of those whom Moses sent to search the land in the second year after the Exodus. He was one of the family chiefs of the tribe of Judah. He and Joshua the son of Nun were the only two of the whole number who encouraged the people to go up and possess…

jephunneh_840.name: Jephunneh
jephunneh_840.description: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

igal_1598.name: Igal
igal_1598.description: Num. 13:7, one of the spies of the tribe of Issachar.

palti_2269.name: Palti
palti_2269.description: Deliverance from the Lord, one of the spies representing the tribe of Benjamin (Num. 13:9).

raphu_2397.name: Raphu
raphu_2397.description: Healed, a Benjamite, whose son Palti was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:9).

gaddiel_1265.name: Gaddiel
gaddiel_1265.description: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies (Num. 13:10).

gaddi_1264.name: Gaddi
gaddi_1264.description: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land (Num. 13:11).

susi_2805.name: Susi
susi_2805.description: The father of Gaddi, who was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:11).

ammiel_220.name: Ammiel
ammiel_220.description: One of the twelve spies sent by Moses to search the land of Canaan (Num. 13:12). He was one of the ten who perished by the plague for their unfavourable report (Num. 14:37).

sethur_2505.name: Sethur
sethur_2505.description: Hidden, one of the spies sent to search the Promised Land. He was of the tribe of Asher (Num. 13:13).

michael_2058.name: Michael
michael_2058.description: The father of Sethur, the spy selected to represent Asher (Num. 13:13).

nahbi_2141.name: Nahbi
nahbi_2141.description: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:14).

ahiman_146.name: Ahiman
ahiman_146.description: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron (Num. 13:22) when they went in to explore the land. They were afterwards driven out and slain (Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

talmai_2818.name: Talmai
talmai_2818.description: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

anak_252.name: Anak
anak_252.description: Long-necked, the son of Arba, father of the Anakim (Josh. 15:13; 21:11, Heb. Anok).

dathan_982.name: Dathan
dathan_982.description: Welled; belonging to a fountain, a son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who joined Korah (q.v.) in his conspiracy, and with his accomplices was swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1; 26:9; Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:17).

abiram_47.name: Abiram (son of Eliab)
abiram_47.description: One of the sons of Eliab, who joined Korah in the conspiracy against Moses and Aaron. He and all the conspirators, with their families and possessions (except the children of Korah), were swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1-27; 26:9; Ps. 106:17).

eliab_1074.name: Eliab
eliab_1074.description: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

peleth_2311.name: Peleth
peleth_2311.description: A Reubenite whose son was one of the conspirators against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1).

arad_281.name: Arad
arad_281.description: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

sihon_2739.name: Sihon
sihon_2739.description: Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them. The Israelites went forth against him to battle, and gained a complete victory.…

chemosh_931.name: Chemosh
chemosh_931.description: The destroyer, subduer, or fish-god, the god of the Moabites (Num. 21:29; Jer. 48:7, 13, 46). The worship of this god, “the abomination of Moab,” was introduced at Jerusalem by Solomon (1 Kings 11:7), but was abolished by Josiah (2 Kings 23:13). On the “Moabite Stone” (q.v.), Mesha (2 Kings 3:5) ascribes his victories…

og_2238.name: Og
og_2238.description: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13). His bedstead (or rather sarcophagus) was of iron (or ironstone),…

balak_387.name: Balak
balak_387.description: Empty; spoiler, a son of Zippor, and king of the Moabites (Num. 22:2, 4). From fear of the Israelites, who were encamped near the confines of his territory, he applied to Balaam (q.v.) to curse them; but in vain (Josh. 24:9).

zippor_3094.name: Zippor
zippor_3094.description: A little bird, the father of Balak, king of Moab (Num. 22:2, 4).

balaam_593.name: Balaam
balaam_593.description: Lord of the people; foreigner or glutton, as interpreted by others, the son of Beor, was a man of some rank among the Midianites (Num. 31:8; comp. 16). He resided at Pethor (Deut. 23:4), in Mesopotamia (Num. 23:7). It is evident that though dwelling among idolaters he had some knowledge of the true God; and was held…

beor_466.name: Beor
beor_466.description: The father of Balaam (Num. 22:5; 24:3, 15; 31:8). In 2 Pet. 2:15 he is called Bosor.

baal_573.name: Baal
baal_573.description: The name appropriated to the principal male god of the Phoenicians. It is found in several places in the plural BAALIM (Judg. 2:11; 10:10; 1 Kings 18:18; Jer. 2:23; Hos. 2:17). Baal is identified with Molech (Jer. 19:5). It was known to the Israelites as Baal-peor (Num. 25:3; Deut. 4:3), was worshipped till the time…

agag_108.name: Agag
agag_108.description: A king of the Amalekites referred to by Balaam (Num. 24:7). He lived at the time of the Exodus.

nemuel_2177.name: Nemuel
nemuel_2177.description: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

abiezer_763.name: Abiezer
abiezer_763.description: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2). He was also called Jeezer (Num. 26:30).

zelophehad_3035.name: Zelophehad
zelophehad_3035.description: First-born, of the tribe of Manasseh, and of the family of Gilead; died in the wilderness. Having left no sons, his daughters, concerned lest their father’s name should be “done away from among his family,” made an appeal to Moses, who, by divine direction, appointed it as “a statute of judgment” in Israel that…

mahlah_1895.name: Mahlah
mahlah_1895.description: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

noah_2211.name: Noah (daughter of Zelophehad)
noah_2211.description: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second…

hoglah_1548.name: Hoglah
hoglah_1548.description: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

tirzah_2868.name: Tirzah
tirzah_2868.description: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

ard_294.name: Ard
ard_294.description: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin (Num. 26:38-40). In 1 Chr. 8:3 he is called Addar. His descendants are mentioned in Num. 26:40.

rekem_2418.name: Rekem
rekem_2418.description: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites destroyed (Num. 31:8).

zur_3110.name: Zur
zur_3110.description: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites defeated and put to death (Num. 31:8).

hur_1572.name: Hur
hur_1572.description: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

reba_2400.name: Reba
reba_2400.description: Fourth, one of the Midianite chiefs slain by the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 31:8; Josh. 13:21).

shemuel_2653.name: Shemuel
shemuel_2653.description: The son of Ammihud. He represented Simeon in the division of the land (Num. 34:20).

elidad_1103.name: Elidad
elidad_1103.description: Whom God has loved, son of Chislon, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin; one of those who were appointed to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (Num. 34:21).

hanniel_1401.name: Hanniel
hanniel_1401.description: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 34:23).

kemuel_1774.name: Kemuel
kemuel_1774.description: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

shiphtan_2711.name: Shiphtan
shiphtan_2711.description: Judicial, an Ephraimite prince at the time of the division of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

paltiel_2270.name: Paltiel
paltiel_2270.description: Deliverance of God, the prince of Issachar who assisted “to divide the land by inheritance” (Num. 34:26).

ahihud_133.name: Ahihud
ahihud_133.description: Name different in Hebrew, meaning brother of Judah. Chief of the tribe of Asher; one of those appointed by Moses to superintend the division of Canaan among the tribe (Num. 34:27).

pedahel_2290.name: Pedahel
pedahel_2290.description: Redeemed of God, the son of Ammihud, a prince of Naphtali (Num. 34:28).

rahab_2388.name: Rahab
rahab_2388.description:
Insolence; pride, a poetical name applied to Egypt in Ps. 87:4; 89:10; Isa. 51:9, as “the proud one.”

 Rahab, (Heb. Rahab; i.e., “broad,” “large”). When the Hebrews were encamped at Shittim, in the “Arabah” or Jordan valley opposite Jericho, ready to cross the river, Joshua, as a final preparation, sent out two spies…

achan_61.name: Achan
achan_61.description: Called also Achar, i.e., one who troubles (1 Chr. 2:7), in commemoration of his crime, which brought upon him an awful destruction (Josh. 7:1). On the occasion of the fall of Jericho, he seized, contrary to the divine command, an ingot of gold, a quantity of silver, and a costly Babylonish garment, which he hid in his…

carmi_921.name: Carmi
carmi_921.description: The son of Zimri, and the father of Achan (Josh. 7:1), “the troubler of Israel.”

zabdi_2954.name: Zabdi
zabdi_2954.description: An ancestor of Achan (Josh. 7:1, 17, 18). He is probably the “Zimri” of 1 Chr. 2:6.

hoham_1549.name: Hoham
hoham_1549.description: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Josh. 10:3, 5, 16-27).

japhia_727.name: Japhia
japhia_727.description: The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Josh. 10:33).

debir_995.name: Debir
debir_995.description: The king of Eglon, one of the five Canaanitish kings who were hanged by Joshua (Josh. 10:3, 23) after the victory at Gibeon. These kings fled and took refuge in a cave at Makkedah. Here they were kept confined till Joshua returned from the pursuit of their discomfited armies, when he caused them to be brought forth,…

jasher_737.name: Jasher
