shethar-boznai_2674.description: Star of splendour, a Persian officer who vainly attempted to hinder the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:3, 6; 6:6, 13).

artaxerxes_314.name: Artaxerxes
artaxerxes_314.description: The king mentioned in Ezra 7:1, in the seventh year (B.C. 458) of whose reign Ezra led a second colony of Jews back to Jerusalem, was probably Longimanus, who reigned for forty years (B.C. 464-425); the grandson of Darius, who, fourteen years later, permitted Nehemiah to return and rebuild Jerusalem.

ezra_1245.name: Ezra
ezra_1245.description: The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name. He was the son, or perhaps grandson, of Seraiah (2 Kings 25:18-21), and a lineal descendant of Phinehas, the son of Aaron (Ezra 7:1-5). All we know of his personal…

gershom_1304.name: Gershom
gershom_1304.description: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).

obadiah_2224.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2224.description: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon (Ezra 8:9).

ariel_302.name: Ariel
ariel_302.description: One of the chief men sent by Ezra to procure Levites for the sanctuary (Ezra 8:16).

jarib_733.name: Jarib
jarib_733.description: One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16).

joiarib_1682.name: Joiarib
joiarib_1682.description: Ezra 8:16, a “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

hashabiah_1434.name: Hashabiah
hashabiah_1434.description: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

meremoth_2006.name: Meremoth
meremoth_2006.description: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3), to whom were sent the sacred vessels (Ezra 8:33) belonging to the temple. He took part in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

urijah_2899.name: Urijah
urijah_2899.description: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

eleazar_1066.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1066.description: A son of Phinehas associated with the priests in taking charge of the sacred vessels brought back to Jerusalem after the Exile (Ezra 8:33).

noadiah_2208.name: Noadiah
noadiah_2208.description: A Levite who returned from Babylon (Ezra 8:33).

shechaniah_2586.name: Shechaniah
shechaniah_2586.description: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

nehemiah_2172.name: Nehemiah
nehemiah_2172.description: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan. The king, Artaxerxes Longimanus, seems to have…

hanani_1382.name: Hanani
hanani_1382.description: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem. Nehemiah afterwards appointed him to have charge of the city gates.

asaph_332.name: Asaph
asaph_332.description: The “keeper of the king’s forest,” to whom Nehemiah requested from Artaxerxes a “letter” that he might give him timber for the temple at Jerusalem (Neh. 2:8).

sanballat_2470.name: Sanballat
sanballat_2470.description: Held some place of authority in Samaria when Nehemiah went up to Jerusalem to rebuild its ruined walls. He vainly attempted to hinder this work (Neh. 2:10, 19; 4:1-12; 6). His daughter became the wife of one of the sons of Joiada, a son of the high priest, much to the grief of Nehemiah (13:28).

tobiah_2872.name: Tobiah
tobiah_2872.description: Pleasing to Jehovah, the “servant,” the “Ammonite,” who joined with those who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Exile (Neh. 2:10). He was a man of great influence, which he exerted in opposition to the Jews, and “sent letters” to Nehemiah “to put him in fear” (Neh. 6:17-19). “Eliashib the priest” prepared…

geshem_1307.name: Geshem
geshem_1307.description: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon (Neh. 2:19; 6:1, 2). He united with Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.

zadok_2976.name: Zadok
zadok_2976.description: The sons of Baana, one of those who assisted in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

jadon_688.name: Jadon
jadon_688.description: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

harhaiah_1413.name: Harhaiah
harhaiah_1413.description: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

jedaiah_754.name: Jedaiah
jedaiah_754.description: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

zabbai_2952.name: Zabbai
zabbai_2952.description: The father of Baruch, who “earnestly repaired” part of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:20; marg., “Zaccai”).

shemaiah_2637.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2637.description: A false prophet who hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Neh. 6:10).

mehetabeel_1979.name: Mehetabeel
mehetabeel_1979.description: Whose benefactor is God, the father of Delaiah, and grandfather of Shemaiah, who joined Sanballat against Nehemiah (Neh. 6:10).

noadiah_2209.name: Noadiah
noadiah_2209.description: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews (Neh. 6:14). Being bribed by them, she tried to stir up discontent among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and so to embarrass Nehemiah in his great work of rebuilding the ruined walls of the city.

hananiah_1391.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1391.description: The “ruler of the palace; he was a faithful man, and feared God above many” (Neh. 7:2).

mattithiah_1976.name: Mattithiah
mattithiah_1976.description: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law (Neh. 8:4).

shema_2617.name: Shema
shema_2617.description: One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

urijah_2904.name: Urijah
urijah_2904.description: One of the priests who stood at the right hand of Ezra’s pulpit when he read and expounded the law (Neh. 8:4).

malchiah_1906.name: Malchiah
malchiah_1906.description: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” (Neh. 8:4).

hashum_1447.name: Hashum
hashum_1447.description: Stood on Ezra’s left hand while he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

hashbadana_1441.name: Hashbadana
hashbadana_1441.description: Consideration in judging, stood at Ezra’s left hand when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

meshullam_2033.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2033.description: One of the principal Israelites who supported Ezra when expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:4).

hodijah_1545.name: Hodijah
hodijah_1545.description: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

kelita_1772.name: Kelita
kelita_1772.description: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:7; 10:10).

hanan_1374.name: Hanan
hanan_1374.description: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

pelaiah_2302.name: Pelaiah
pelaiah_2302.description: A Levite who expounded the law (Neh. 8:7).

hashabniah_1440.name: Hashabniah
hashabniah_1440.description: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

zidkijah_3077.name: Zidkijah
zidkijah_3077.description: The Lord is righteous, one who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh. 10:1).

hattush_1460.name: Hattush
hattush_1460.description: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

shebaniah_2574.name: Shebaniah
shebaniah_2574.description: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

malluch_1921.name: Malluch
malluch_1921.description: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

miniamin_2077.name: Miniamin
miniamin_2077.description: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

bilgah_501.name: Bilgah
bilgah_501.description: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5, 18).

adonijah_99.name: Adonijah
adonijah_99.description: One of the “chiefs of the people” after the Captivity (Neh. 10:16).

azzur_572.name: Azzur
azzur_572.description: One of those who sealed the covenant with Jehovah on the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:17).

hodijah_1547.name: Hodijah
hodijah_1547.description: Neh. 10:18, a Levite who sealed the covenant.

hezir_1517.name: Hezir
hezir_1517.description: Neh. 10:20, one who sealed Nehemiah’s covenant.

jaddua_686.name: Jaddua
jaddua_686.description: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21).

hanan_1375.name: Hanan
hanan_1375.description: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:22).

anan_255.name: Anan
anan_255.description: Cloud, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:26).

zabdiel_2958.name: Zabdiel
zabdiel_2958.description: An overseer of the priests after the Captivity (Neh. 11:14).

uzzi_2921.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2921.description: A son of Bani. He had the oversight of the Levites after the return from captivity (Neh. 11:22).

pethahiah_2322.name: Pethahiah
pethahiah_2322.description: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

ezra_1246.name: Ezra
ezra_1246.description: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

unni_2892.name: Unni
unni_2892.description: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 12:9).

joiakim_1681.name: Joiakim
joiakim_1681.description: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

eliashib_1100.name: Eliashib
eliashib_1100.description: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21). His indulgence of Tobiah the Ammonite provoked the indignation of Nehemiah (13:4, 7).

jaddua_687.name: Jaddua
jaddua_687.description: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

meraiah_2002.name: Meraiah
meraiah_2002.description: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

helkai_1485.name: Helkai
helkai_1485.description: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

uzzi_2922.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2922.description: The head of the house of Jedaiah, one of “the chief of the priests” (Neh. 12:19).

eber_1032.name: Eber (Amok Family Head)
eber_1032.description: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

darius_979.name: Darius
darius_979.description: Darius the Persian (Neh. 12:22) was probably the Darius II. (Ochus or Nothus) of profane history, the son of Artaxerxes Longimanus, who was the son and successor of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). There are some, however, who think that the king here meant was Darius III. (Codomannus), the antagonist of Alexander the Great (B.C.…

milalai_2081.name: Milalai
milalai_2081.description: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

nethaneel_2197.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2197.description: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

uzzi_2923.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2923.description: A priest who assisted in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

malchijah_1914.name: Malchijah
malchijah_1914.description: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

zadok_2979.name: Zadok
zadok_2979.description: “The scribe” set over the treasuries of the temple by Nehemiah along with a priest and a Levite (Neh. 13:13).

vashti_2937.name: Vashti
vashti_2937.description: Beautiful, the queen of Ahasuerus, who was deposed from her royal dignity because she refused to obey the king when he desired her to appear in the banqueting hall of Shushan the palace (Esther 1:10-12).

mehuman_1984.name: Mehuman
mehuman_1984.description: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti (Esther 1:10).

harbona_1410.name: Harbona
harbona_1410.description: (a Persian word meaning “ass-driver”), one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains of king Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10; 7:9).

bigtha_494.name: Bigtha
bigtha_494.description: Garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains who had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10).

abagtha_3.name: Abagtha
abagtha_3.description: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus’s court (Esther 1:10; 2:21).

shethar_2673.name: Shethar
shethar_2673.description: A star, a prince at the court of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:14).

memucan_1995.name: Memucan
memucan_1995.description: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

hegai_1477.name: Hegai
hegai_1477.description: Eunuch, had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8).

mordecai_2107.name: Mordecai
mordecai_2107.description: The son of Jair, of the tribe of Benjamin. It has been alleged that he was carried into captivity with Jeconiah, and hence that he must have been at least one hundred and twenty-nine years old in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). But the words of Esther do not necessarily lead to this conclusion. It was probably…

jair_710.name: Jair
jair_710.description: A Benjamite, the father of Mordecai, Esther’s uncle (Esther 2:5).

esther_1343.name: Esther
esther_1343.description: The queen of Ahasuerus, and heroine of the book that bears her name. She was a Jewess named Hadas’sah (the myrtle), but when she entered the royal harem she received the name by which she henceforth became known (Esther 2:7). It is a Syro-Arabian modification of the Persian word satarah, which means a star. She was…

shaashgaz_2508.name: Shaashgaz
shaashgaz_2508.description: Servant of the beautiful, a chief eunuch in the second house of the harem of king Ahasuerus (Esther 2:14).

abihail_32.name: Abihail
abihail_32.description: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15).

bigthana_495.name: Bigthana
bigthana_495.description: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life. Mordecai detected the conspiracy, and the culprits were hanged (Esther 2:21-23; 6:1-3).

teresh_2842.name: Teresh
teresh_2842.description: Severe, a eunuch or chamberlain in the palace of Ahasuerus, who conspired with another to murder him. The plot was detected by Mordecai, and the conspirators were put to death (Esther 2:21; 6:2).

haman_1360.name: Haman
haman_1360.description: (of Persian origin), magnificent, the name of the vizier (i.e., the prime minister) of the Persian king Ahasuerus (Esther 3:1, etc.). He is called an “Agagite,” which seems to denote that he was descended from the royal family of the Amalekites, the bitterest enemies of the Jews, as Agag was one of the titles of the…

hammedatha_1362.name: Hammedatha
hammedatha_1362.description: Father of Haman, designated usually “the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, 10; 8:5).

hatach_1452.name: Hatach
hatach_1452.description: Verity, one of the eunuchs or chamberlains in the palace of Ahasuerus (Esther 4:5, 6, 9, 10).

zeresh_3049.name: Zeresh
zeresh_3049.description: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5:10).

parshandatha_2277.name: Parshandatha
parshandatha_2277.description: An interpreter of the law, the eldest of Haman’s sons, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:7).

parmashta_2271.name: Parmashta
parmashta_2271.description: Strong-fisted, a son of Haman, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:9).

vajezatha_2935.name: Vajezatha
vajezatha_2935.description: Purity; worthy of honour, one of Haman’s sons, whom the Jews slew in the palace of Shushan (Esther 9:9).

job_1639.name: Job
job_1639.description: Persecuted, an Arabian patriarch who resided in the land of Uz (q.v.). While living in the midst of great prosperity, he was suddenly overwhelmed by a series of sore trials that fell upon him. Amid all his sufferings he maintained his integrity. Once more God visited him with the rich tokens of his goodness and even…

bildad_499.name: Bildad
bildad_499.description: Son of contention, one of Job’s friends. He is called “the Shuhite,” probably as belonging to Shuah, a district in Arabia, in which Shuah, the sixth son of Abraham by Keturah, settled (Gen. 25:2). He took part in each of the three controversies into which Job’s friends entered with him (Job 8:1; 18:1; 25:1), and…

zophar_3105.name: Zophar
zophar_3105.description: Chirping, one of Job’s friends who came to condole with him in his distress (Job 2:11. The LXX. render here “king of the Mineans” = Ma’in, Maonites, Judg. 10:12, in Southern Arabia). He is called a Naamathite, or an inhabitant of some unknown place called Naamah.

elihu_1130.name: Elihu
elihu_1130.description: “The son of Barachel, a Buzite” (Job 32:2), one of Job’s friends. When the debate between Job and his friends is brought to a close, Elihu for the first time makes his appearance, and delivers his opinion on the points at issue (Job 32-37).

barachel_400.name: Barachel
barachel_400.description: Whom God has blessed, a Buzite, the father of Elihu, one of Job’s friends (Job 32:2, 6).

ram_2393.name: Ram
ram_2393.description: A person mentioned in Job 32:2 as founder of a clan to which Elihu belonged. The same as Aram of Gen. 22:21.

jemima_837.name: Jemima
jemima_837.description: Dove, the eldest of Job’s three daughters born after his time of trial (Job 42:14).

keren-happuch_1780.name: Keren-happuch
keren-happuch_1780.description: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter (Job. 42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

agur_112.name: Agur
agur_112.description: Gatherer; the collector, mentioned as author of the sayings in Prov. 30. Nothing is known of him beyond what is there recorded.

jakeh_712.name: Jakeh
jakeh_712.description: Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

ucal_2887.name: Ucal
ucal_2887.description: The name of a person to whom Agur’s words are addressed (Prov. 30:1).

lemuel_1817.name: Lemuel
lemuel_1817.description: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed (Prov. 31:1-9). Nothing is certainly known concerning him. The rabbis identified him with Solomon.

tabeal_2808.name: Tabeal
tabeal_2808.description: Goodness of God, the father of one whom the kings of Syria and Samaria in vain attempted to place on the throne of Ahaz (Isa. 7:6).

maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.description: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa. 8:1, 3), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the Assyrian army.

lucifer_1832.name: Lucifer
lucifer_1832.description: Brilliant star, a title given to the king of Babylon (Isa. 14:12) to denote his glory.

merodach-baladan_483.name: Merodach-baladan
merodach-baladan_483.description: Merodach has given a son, (Isa. 39:1), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.” One bearing this name sent ambassadors to…

maaseiah_1866.name: Maaseiah
maaseiah_1866.description: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

micah_2053.name: Micah
micah_2053.description: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15). Very little is known of the circumstances of his life (comp. Jer. 26:18, 19).

urijah_2905.name: Urijah
urijah_2905.description: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23). He fled into Egypt from the cruelty of the king, but having been brought back he was beheaded and his body “cast into the graves of the common people.”

shemaiah_2642.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2642.description: The father of Urijah the prophet (Jer. 26:20).

azur_569.name: Azur
azur_569.description: The father of Hananiah, a false prophet (Jer. 28:1).

elasah_1056.name: Elasah
elasah_1056.description: The son of Shaphan, one of the two who were sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and also took charge of Jeremiah’s letter to the captives in Babylon (Jer. 29:3).

gemariah_1295.name: Gemariah
gemariah_1295.description: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon (Jer. 29:3, 4).

ahab_114.name: Ahab
ahab_114.description: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah (Jer. 29:21), of whom nothing further is known.

shemaiah_2643.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2643.description: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

hanameel_1369.name: Hanameel
hanameel_1369.description: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

shallum_2525.name: Shallum
shallum_2525.description: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

baruch_410.name: Baruch
baruch_410.description: The secretary of the prophet Jeremiah (32:12; 36:4). He was of the tribe of Judah (51:59). To him Jeremiah dictated his prophecies regarding the invasion of the Babylonians and the Captivity. These he read to the people from a window in the temple in the fourth year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 36).…

jaazaniah_668.name: Jaazaniah
jaazaniah_668.description: The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3).

gemariah_1296.name: Gemariah
gemariah_1296.description: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer. 36:11-20), which filled him with terror. He joined with others…

michaiah_2072.name: Michaiah
michaiah_2072.description: The son of Gemariah. He reported to the king’s officers Jeremiah’s prediction, which he had heard Baruch read (Jer. 36:11, 13) from his father Gemariah’s chamber in the temple.

delaiah_1004.name: Delaiah
delaiah_1004.description: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

shemaiah_2644.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2644.description: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

zedekiah_3032.name: Zedekiah
zedekiah_3032.description: The son of Hananiah, a prince of Judah in the days of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

jehudi_823.name: Jehudi
jehudi_823.description: A Jew, son of Nethaniah. He was sent by the princes to invite Baruch to read Jeremiah’s roll to them (Jer. 36:14, 21).

hammelech_1363.name: Hammelech
hammelech_1363.description: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son. Probably, however, it is to be taken as a proper name.

abdeel_5.name: Abdeel
abdeel_5.description: Servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.

jucal_822.name: Jucal
jucal_822.description: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal (Jer. 38:1). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom (Jer. 37:3) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar. He was accompanied by Zephaniah (q.v.).

shelemiah_2600.name: Shelemiah
shelemiah_2600.description: Father of one of those who accused Jeremiah to Zedekiah (Jer. 37:3; 38:1).

shelemiah_2601.name: Shelemiah
shelemiah_2601.description: Father of a captain of the ward (Jer. 37:13).

hananiah_1397.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1397.description: Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah (Jer. 37:13).

shephatiah_2664.name: Shephatiah
shephatiah_2664.description: One of the princes who urged the putting of Jeremiah to death (Jer. 38:1-4).

gedaliah_1290.name: Gedaliah
gedaliah_1290.description: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah (Jer. 38:1).

nergal-sharezer_2183.name: Nergal-sharezer
nergal-sharezer_2183.description: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.” He was a Babylonian grandee of high rank. From profane history and the inscriptions, we are led to conclude that he was the Neriglissar who murdered…

samgar-nebo_2466.name: Samgar-nebo
samgar-nebo_2466.description: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

nebushasban_2168.name: Nebushasban
nebushasban_2168.description: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon. He was one of those whom the king sent to release Jeremiah from prison in Jerusalem (Jer. 39:13).

baalis_578.name: Baalis
baalis_578.description: King of the Ammonites at the time of the Babylonian captivity (Jer. 40:14). He hired Ishmael to slay Gedaliah who had been appointed governor over the cities of Judah.

seraiah_2500.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2500.description: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion. Jeremiah took advantage of the occasion, and sent with Seraiah a word of cheer to the exiles in Babylon, and an announcement of the doom in store for that…

ezekiel_1237.name: Ezekiel
ezekiel_1237.description: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.” He was probably carried away captive with Jehoiachin (1:2; 2 Kings 24:14-16) about B.C. 597. His prophetic call came to him “in the…

pelatiah_2307.name: Pelatiah
pelatiah_2307.description: One of the twenty-five princes of the people against whom Ezekiel prophesied on account of their wicked counsel (Ezek. 11:1-13).

daniel_975.name: Daniel
daniel_975.description: Beltis protect the king!, the Chaldee name given to Daniel by Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:7).

aholibah_171.name: Aholibah
aholibah_171.description: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations. (Ezek. 23:4, 11, 22, 36, 44).

ashpenaz_339.name: Ashpenaz
ashpenaz_339.description: The master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:3), the “Rabsaris” of the court. His position was similar to that of the Kislar-aga of the modern Turkish sultans.

shadrach_1398.name: Shadrach
shadrach_1398.description: Aku’s command, the Chaldean name given to Hananiah, one of the Hebrew youths whom Nebuchadnezzar carried captive to Babylon (Dan. 1:6, 7; 3:12-30). He and his two companions refused to bow down before the image which Nebuchadnezzar had set up on the plains of Dura. Their conduct filled the king with the greatest fury,…

meshach_2092.name: Meshach
meshach_2092.description: One of the three Hebrew youths who were trained with Daniel in Babylon (Dan. 1:11, 19), and promoted to the rank of Magi. He and his companions were afterwards cast into the burning fiery furnace for refusing to worship the idol the king had set up, from which they were miraculously delivered (3:13-30). His Chaldean…

azariah_545.name: Azariah
azariah_545.description: The original name of Abed-nego (Dan. 1:6, 7, 11, 16). He was of the royal family of Judah, and with his other two companions remarkable for his personal beauty and his intelligence as well as piety.

melzar_1994.name: Melzar
melzar_1994.description: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

belshazzar_437.name: Belshazzar
belshazzar_437.description: Bel protect the king!, the last of the kings of Babylon (Dan. 5:1). He was the son of Nabonidus by Nitocris, who was the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar and the widow of Nergal-sharezer. When still young he made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and when heated with wine sent for the sacred vessels his “father”…

gabriel_1261.name: Gabriel
gabriel_1261.description:
Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27).

 He announced also the birth of John the Baptist (Luke 1:11), and of the Messiah (26). He describes…

michael_2068.name: Michael
michael_2068.description: The title given to one of the chief angels (Dan. 10:13, 21; 12:1). He had special charge of Israel as a nation. He disputed with Satan (Jude 1:9) about the body of Moses. He is also represented as warning against “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world” (Rev. 12:7-9).

hosea_1555.name: Hosea
hosea_1555.description: Salvation, the son of Beeri, and author of the book of prophecies bearing his name. He belonged to the kingdom of Israel. “His Israelitish origin is attested by the peculiar, rough, Aramaizing diction, pointing to the northern part of Palestine; by the intimate acquaintance he evinces with the localities of Ephraim…

diblaim_1009.name: Diblaim
diblaim_1009.description: Doubled cakes, the mother of Gomer, who was Hosea’s wife (Hos. 1:3).

lo-ruhamah_1829.name: Lo-ruhamah
lo-ruhamah_1829.description: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people (Hos. 1:6; 2:23).

lo-ammi_1827.name: Lo-ammi
lo-ammi_1827.description: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people (Hos. 1:9, 10), his treatment of them as a foreign people. This Hebrew word is rendered by “not my people” in ver. 10; 2:23.

joel_1660.name: Joel
joel_1660.description: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel. His personal history is only known from his book.

pethuel_2323.name: Pethuel
pethuel_2323.description: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

amos_238.name: Amos
amos_238.description: Borne; a burden, one of the twelve minor prophets. He was a native of Tekota, the modern Tekua, a town about 12 miles south-east of Bethlehem. He was a man of humble birth, neither a “prophet nor a prophet’s son,” but “an herdman and a dresser of sycomore trees,” R.V. He prophesied in the days of Uzziah, king of…

amaziah_217.name: Amaziah
amaziah_217.description: A priest of the golden calves at Bethel (Amos 7:10-17).

helem_1479.name: Helem
helem_1479.description: Zech. 6:10, one who returned from Babylon.

josiah_1731.name: Josiah
josiah_1731.description: Common in later times among the Jews in Palestine (Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34). It is noticeable that this familiar bird is only mentioned in these passages in connection with our Lord’s lamentation over the impenitence of Jerusalem.

zephaniah_3041.name: Zephaniah
zephaniah_3041.description: The father of Josiah, the priest who dwelt in Jerusalem when Darius issued the decree that the temple should be rebuilt (Zech. 6:10).

sherezer_2670.name: Sherezer
sherezer_2670.description: One of the messengers whom the children of the Captivity sent to Jerusalem “to pray for them before the Lord” (Zech. 7:2).

regem-melech_2408.name: Regem-melech
regem-melech_2408.description: Friend of the king, one of the two messengers sent by the exiled Jews to Jerusalem in the time of Darius (Zech. 7:2) to make inquiries at the temple.

malachi_1899.name: Malachi
malachi_1899.description: Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon (Mal. 4:4, 5, 6). Nothing is known of him beyond what is contained in his book of prophecies. Some have supposed that the name is simply a title descriptive of his character as a messenger of Jehovah, and not…

rachab_2385.name: Rachab
rachab_2385.description: '=Rahab, a name found in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:5).

abiud_56.name: Abiud
abiud_56.description: A descendant of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim (Matt. 1:13, “Abiud”); called also Juda (Luke 3:26), and Obadiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

eliakim_1087.name: Eliakim
eliakim_1087.description: The son of Abiud, of the posterity of Zerubbabel (Matt. 1:13).

sadoc_2454.name: Sadoc
sadoc_2454.description: Just, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:14).

matthan_1968.name: Matthan
matthan_1968.description: The son of Eleazar, and father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary (Matt. 1:15).

joseph_1715.name: Joseph (Mary's Husband)
joseph_1715.description: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.” He was by trade a carpenter (Matt. 13:55). He is last mentioned in connection with the journey to Jerusalem, when Jesus was twelve years old. It is probable that he died before Jesus entered on…

mary_1938.name: Mary (Mother of Jesus)
mary_1938.description: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history. Her genealogy is given in Luke 3. She was of the tribe of Judah and the lineage of David (Ps. 132:11; Luke 1:32). She was connected by marriage…

archelaus_291.name: Archelaus
archelaus_291.description: Ruler of the people, son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, a Samaritan woman. He was educated along with his brother Antipas at Rome. He inherited from his father a third part of his kingdom viz., Idumea, Judea, and Samaria, and hence is called “king” (Matt. 2:22). It was for fear of him that Joseph and Mary turned…

john_1676.name: John the Baptist
john_1676.description: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent. His father, Zacharias, was a priest of the course of Abia (1 Chr. 24:10), and his mother, Elisabeth, was of the daughters of Aaron (Luke 1:5). The mission of John was the subject of prophecy…

peter_2745.name: Simon Peter
peter_2745.description: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture. He had a younger brother called Andrew, who first brought him to Jesus (John 1:40-42). His native town was Bethsaida, on the western coast…

andrew_264.name: Andrew
andrew_264.description: Manliness, a Greek name; one of the apostles of our Lord. He was of Bethsaida in Galilee (John 1:44), and was the brother of Simon Peter (Matt. 4:18; 10:2). On one occasion John the Baptist, whose disciple he then was, pointing to Jesus, said, “Behold the Lamb of God” (John 1:40); and Andrew, hearing him, immediately…

james_717.name: James (Son of Zebedee)
james_717.description: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56). With John and Peter he was present at the transfiguration (Matt. 17:1; Mark 9:2), at the raising of Jairus’s daughter (Mark 5:37-43), and in the…

zebedee_2998.name: Zebedee
zebedee_2998.description: A Galilean fisherman, the husband of Salome (q.v.), and the father of James and John, two of our Lord’s disciples (Matt. 4:21; 27:56; Mark 15:40). He seems to have been a man of some position in Capernaum, for he had two boats (Luke 5:4) and “hired servants” (Mark 1:20) of his own. No mention is made of him after the…

john_1677.name: John the Apostle
john_1677.description: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida. His father was apparently a man of some wealth (comp. Mark 1:20; Luke 5:3; John 19:27). He…

mother_of_the_wife_of_simon_2111.name: Mother of the Wife of Simon

matthew_1971.name: Matthew
matthew_1971.description: Gift of God, a common Jewish name after the Exile. He was the son of Alphaeus, and was a publican or tax-gatherer at Capernaum. On one occasion Jesus, coming up from the side of the lake, passed the custom-house where Matthew was seated, and said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew arose and followed him, and became his…

philip_2344.name: Phillip the Apostle
philip_2344.description: One of the twelve apostles; a native of Bethsaida, “the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). He readily responded to the call of Jesus when first addressed to him (43), and forthwith brought Nathanael also to Jesus (45, 46). He seems to have held a prominent place among the apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; John…

bartholomew_405.name: Bartholomew
bartholomew_405.description: Son of Tolmai, one of the twelve apostles (Matt. 10:3; Acts 1:13); generally supposed to have been the same as Nathanael. In the synoptic gospels Philip and Bartholomew are always mentioned together, while Nathanael is never mentioned; in the fourth gospel, on the other hand, Philip and Nathanael are similarly…

thomas_2851.name: Thomas
thomas_2851.description: Twin, one of the twelve (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18, etc.). He was also called Didymus (John 11:16; 20:24), which is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew name. All we know regarding him is recorded in the fourth Gospel (John 11:15, 16; 14:4, 5; 20:24, 25, 26-29). From the circumstance that in the lists of the apostles he is…

james_718.name: James (Son of Alphaeus)
james_718.description: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15). He had a separate interview with our Lord after his…

alphaeus_192.name: Alphaeus
alphaeus_192.description: The father of James the Less, the apostle and writer of the epistle (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13), and the husband of Mary (John 19:25). The Hebrew form of this name is Cleopas, or Clopas (q.v.).

lebbaeus_1815.name: Lebbaeus Thaddaeus
lebbaeus_1815.description: Breast, the name of one of the apostles (Mark 3:18), called “Lebbaeus” in Matt. 10:3, and in Luke 6:16, “Judas the brother of James;” while John (14:22), probably referring to the same person, speaks of “Judas, not Iscariot.” These different names all designate the same person, viz., Jude or Judas, the author of the…

simon_2746.name: Simon Zelotes
simon_2746.description: One of the twelve apostles, called the Canaanite (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:18). This word “Canaanite” does not mean a native of Canaan, but is derived from the Syriac word Kanean or Kaneniah, which was the name of a Jewish sect. The Revised Version has “Cananaean;” marg., “or Zealot” He is also called “Zelotes” (Luke 6:15;…

judas_1760.name: Judas Iscariot
judas_1760.description: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels. The evil of his nature probably gradually unfolded itself till “Satan entered into him” (John 13:27), and he…

james_719.name: James (Brother of Jesus)
james_719.description: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15). He had a separate interview with our Lord after his…

simon_2747.name: Simon
simon_2747.description: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).

jude_1756.name: Jude
jude_1756.description: '= Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19). He who is called “the brother of James” (Luke 6:16), may be the same with the Judas…

herod_1505.name: Herod Antipas
herod_1505.description: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

philip_2345.name: Philip
philip_2345.description: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome. (See  HEROD PHILIP I.)

herodias_1507.name: Herodias
herodias_1507.description: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city. She consented to leave her husband and become his wife. Some time after, Herod met John…

caiaphas_532.name: Caiaphas
caiaphas_532.description: The Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) at the beginning of our Lord’s public ministry, in the reign of Tiberius (Luke 3:2), and also at the time of his condemnation and crucifixion (Matt. 26:3, 57; John 11:49; 18:13, 14). He held this office during the whole of Pilate’s administration. His wife was the daughter of Annas,…

simon_2748.name: Simon
simon_2748.description: A leper of Bethany, in whose house Mary anointed our Lord’s head with ointment “as he sat at meat” (Matt. 26:6-13; Mark 14:3-9).

pilate_2365.name: Pontius Pilate
pilate_2365.description: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one. He was the sixth in the order of the Roman procurators of Judea (A.D.…

barabbas_399.name: Barabbas
barabbas_399.description: I.e., son of Abba or of a father, a notorious robber whom Pilate proposed to condemn to death instead of Jesus, whom he wished to release, in accordance with the Roman custom (John 18:40; Mark 15:7; Luke 23:19). But the Jews were so bent on the death of Jesus that they demanded that Barabbas should be pardoned (Matt.…

simon_2749.name: Simon
simon_2749.description: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number. They had a synagogue in Jerusalem for such of their number as went thither to the annual feasts.…

mary_1943.name: Mary Magdalene
mary_1943.description: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.). A mistaken notion has prevailed that this Mary was a woman of bad character, that she was the woman who is emphatically called “a sinner” (Luke…

joseph_1716.name: Joseph (of Arimathea)
joseph_1716.description: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament (1 Sam. 1:19), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim (Matt. 27:57; Luke 23:50), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.” As soon as he heard the tidings of Christ’s death, he “went in boldly” (lit. “having summoned courage,…

alphaeus_193.name: Alphaeus
alphaeus_193.description: The father of Levi, or Matthew (Mark 2:14).

jairus_711.name: Jairus
jairus_711.description: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41). Entering into the chamber of death, accompanied by Peter and James and John and the father and mother of the maiden, he went forward to the bed whereon the corpse lay, and said, Talitha cumi, i.e., “Maid, arise,”…

bartimaeus_406.name: Bartimaeus
bartimaeus_406.description: Son of Timaeus, one of the two blind beggars of Jericho (Mark 10:46; Matt. 20:30). His blindness was miraculously cured on the ground of his faith.

timaeus_2858.name: Timaeus
timaeus_2858.description: Defiled, the father of blind Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46).

alexander_186.name: Alexander
alexander_186.description: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ (Mark 15:21).

salome_2464.name: Salome
salome_2464.description: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25). She sought for her sons places of honour in Christ’s kingdom (Matt. 20:20, 21; comp. 19:28). She witnessed the crucifixion (Mark 15:40), and was present with the other women at the…

theophilus_2849.name: Theophilus
theophilus_2849.description: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1). Nothing beyond this is known of him. From the fact that Luke applies to him the title “most excellent”, the same title Paul uses in addressing Felix (Acts 23:26; 24:3) and Festus (26:25),…

zacharias_2971.name: Zacharias
zacharias_2971.description: A priest of the course of Abia, the eighth of the twenty-four courses into which the priests had been originally divided by David (1 Chr. 23:1-19). Only four of these courses or “families” of the priests returned from the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39); but they were then re-distributed under the old designations. The priests…

elisabeth_1152.name: Elisabeth
elisabeth_1152.description: God her oath, the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:5). She was a descendant of Aaron. She and her husband Zacharias (q.v.) “were both righteous before God” (Luke 1:5, 13). Mary’s visit to Elisabeth is described in 1:39-63.

augustus_366.name: Augustus
augustus_366.description: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born (Luke 2:1). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy (Micah 5:2), in Bethlehem. This name being simply a title meaning “majesty”…

cyrenius_967.name: Cyrenius
cyrenius_967.description: The Grecized form of Quirinus. His full name was Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. Recent historical investigation has proved that Quirinus was governor of Cilicia, which was annexed to Syria at the time of our Lord’s birth. Cilicia, which he ruled, being a province of Syria, he is called the governor, which he was de jure,…

anna_268.name: Anna
anna_268.description: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah (2 Chr. 34:22). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services. When she was eighty-four years old, she entered the temple at the moment when…

phanuel_2327.name: Phanuel
phanuel_2327.description: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna (q.v.), Luke 2:36.

tiberius_2852.name: Tiberius
tiberius_2852.description: I.e., as known in Roman history, Tiberius Claudius Nero, only mentioned in Luke 3:1. He was the stepson of Augustus, whom he succeeded on the throne, A.D. 14. He was noted for his vicious and infamous life. In the fifteenth year of his reign John the Baptist entered on his public ministry, and under him also our Lord…

lysanias_1838.name: Lysanias
lysanias_1838.description: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

annas_269.name: Annas
annas_269.description: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas (Luke 3:2). By the Mosaic law…

heli_1484.name: Heli
heli_1484.description: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

matthat_1969.name: Matthat
matthat_1969.description: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

mattathias_1963.name: Mattathias
mattathias_1963.description: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

maath_1871.name: Maath
maath_1871.description: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

mattathias_1964.name: Mattathias
mattathias_1964.description: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

semei_2488.name: Semei
semei_2488.description: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

joseph_1718.name: Joseph (son of Judah)
joseph_1718.description: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26). Other two of the same name in the ancestry of Christ are also mentioned (3:24, 30).

joanna_1628.name: Joanna
joanna_1628.description: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

rhesa_2438.name: Rhesa
rhesa_2438.description: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

salathiel_2457.name: Salathiel
salathiel_2457.description: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27). The probable explanation of the apparent discrepancy is that he was the son of Neri, the descendant of Nathan, and thus heir to the throne of David on the death of Jeconiah (comp. Jer. 22:30).

melchi_1988.name: Melchi
melchi_1988.description: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

addi_81.name: Addi
addi_81.description: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

levi_1822.name: Levi
levi_1822.description: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

simeon_2743.name: Simeon
simeon_2743.description: One of the ancestors of Joseph (Luke 3:30).

juda_1750.name: Juda
juda_1750.description: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

eliakim_1088.name: Eliakim
eliakim_1088.description: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

melea_1992.name: Melea
melea_1992.description: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

cainan_535.name: Cainan (son of Arphaxad)
cainan_535.description: The son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament. He is usually called the “second Cainan.”

joanna_1629.name: Joanna
joanna_1629.description: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3). She was one of the women who ministered to our Lord, and to whom he appeared after his resurrection (Luke 8:3; 24:10).

susanna_2804.name: Susanna
susanna_2804.description: Lily, with other pious women, ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).

martha_1937.name: Martha
martha_1937.description: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany (Luke 10:38, 40, 41; John 11:1-39). From the residence being called “her house,” some have supposed that she was a widow, and that her brother and sister lodged with her. She seems to have been of an anxious,…

mary_1939.name: Mary (sister of Lazarus)
mary_1939.description: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.” Her character also appears in connection with the death of her…

zacchaeus_2961.name: Zacchaeus
zacchaeus_2961.description: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus being a rich man.” Being short of stature,…

cleophas_950.name: Cleophas
cleophas_950.description: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18). We know nothing definitely regarding him. It is not certain that he was the Clopas of John 19:25, or the Alphaeus of Matt. 10:3, although he may have been so.

jonas_1687.name: Jonas
jonas_1687.description: The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

nathanael_2158.name: Nathanael
nathanael_2158.description: Given or gift of God, one of our Lord’s disciples, “of Cana in Galilee” (John 21:2). He was “an Israelite indeed, in whom was no guile” (1:47, 48). His name occurs only in the Gospel of John, who in his list of the disciples never mentions Bartholomew, with whom he has consequently been identified. He was one of those…

nicodemus_2204.name: Nicodemus
nicodemus_2204.description: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.” He is next met with in the Sanhedrin (7:50-52),…

lazarus_1812.name: Lazarus
lazarus_1812.description: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany. He was raised from the dead after he had lain four days in the tomb (John 11:1-44). This miracle so excited the wrath of the Jews that they sought to put both Jesus and Lazarus to death.

malchus_1916.name: Malchus
malchus_1916.description: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10). But our Lord cured it with a touch (Matt. 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:51). This was the last miracle of bodily cure wrought by our Lord. It is not…

barsabas_1720.name: Barsabas Justus
barsabas_1720.description: Surnamed Barsabas (Acts 1:23); also called Justus. He was one of those who “companied with the apostles all the time that the Lord Jesus went out and in among them” (Acts 1:21), and was one of the candidates for the place of Judas.

john_1678.name: John (Relative of the High Priest)
john_1678.description: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John (Acts 4:6). He was of the kindred of the high priest; otherwise unknown.

alexander_187.name: Alexander (Son of Simon)
alexander_187.description: A relative of Annas the high priest, present when Peter and John were examined before the Sanhedrim (Acts 4:6).

barnabas_1722.name: Barnabas
barnabas_1722.description: Son of consolation, the surname of Joses, a Levite (Acts 4:36). His name stands first on the list of prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch (13:1). Luke speaks of him as a “good man” (11:24). He was born of Jewish parents of the tribe of Levi. He was a native of Cyprus, where he had a possession of land (Acts…

ananias_258.name: Ananias (Husband of Sapphira)
ananias_258.description: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood (Acts 5:5). By common agreement the members of the early Christian community devoted their property to the work of furthering the…

sapphira_2472.name: Sapphira
sapphira_2472.description: Beautiful, the wife of Ananias (q.v.). She was a partner in his guilt and also in his punishment (Acts 5:1-11).

gamaliel_1277.name: Gamaliel
gamaliel_1277.description: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees. He was noted for his learning, and was president of the Sanhedrim during the regins of Tiberius, Caligula, and Claudius, and died, it is said, about eighteen years before the…

theudas_2850.name: Theudas
theudas_2850.description: Thanksgiving, referred to by Gamaliel in his speech before the council at Jerusalem (Acts 5:36). He headed an insurrection against the Roman authority. Beyond this nothing is known of him.

stephen_2802.name: Stephen
stephen_2802.description:
One of the seven deacons, who became a preacher of the gospel. He was the first Christian martyr. His personal character and history are recorded in Acts 6. “He fell asleep” with a prayer for his persecutors on his lips (7:60). Devout men carried him to his grave (8:2).

 It was at the feet of the young Pharisee, Saul…

philip_2347.name: Phillip the Evangelist
philip_2347.description: One of the “seven” (Acts 6:5), called also “the evangelist” (21:8, 9). He was one of those who were “scattered abroad” by the persecution that arose on the death of Stephen. He went first to Samaria, where he laboured as an evangelist with much success (8:5-13). While he was there he received a divine command to…

nicanor_2203.name: Nicanor
nicanor_2203.description: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church (Acts 6:1-6). Nothing further is known of him.

timon_2862.name: Timon
timon_2862.description: Honouring, one of the seven deacons at Jerusalem (Acts 6:5). Nothing further is known of him.

nicolas_2205.name: Nicolas
nicolas_2205.description: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5).

paul_2479.name: Paul
paul_2479.description: '=Saul (q.v.) was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name. He was a native of Tarsus, the capital of Cilicia, a Roman province in the south-east of Asia…

simon_2752.name: Simon the Sorcerer
simon_2752.description: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13). His profession was, however, soon found to be hollow. His conduct called forth from Peter a stern rebuke (8:18-23).…

candace_916.name: Candace
candace_916.description: The queen of the Ethiopians whose “eunuch” or chamberlain was converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27). The country which she ruled was called by the Greeks Meroe, in Upper Nubia. It was long the centre of commercial intercourse between Africa and the south of Asia, and…

ananias_259.name: Ananias (Disciple at Damascus)
ananias_259.description: A Christian at Damascus (Acts 9:10). He became Paul’s instructor; but when or by what means he himself became a Christian we have no information. He was “a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt” at Damascus (22:12).

judas_1758.name: Judas (Jew of Damascus)
judas_1758.description: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent. The street called “Straight” in which it was situated is identified with the modern “street of bazaars,” where is still pointed out the so-called “house of Judas.”

dorcas_2810.name: Dorcas
dorcas_2810.description: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.” And she opened her eyes and sat up; and Peter “gave her his hand, and raised her up;…

simon_2753.name: Simon the Tanner
simon_2753.description: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

cornelius_956.name: Cornelius
cornelius_956.description: A centurion whose history is narrated in Acts 10. He was a “devout man,” and like the centurion of Capernaum, believed in the God of Israel. His residence at Caesrea probably brought him into contact with Jews who communicated to him their expectations regarding the Messiah; and thus he was prepared to welcome the…

agabus_107.name: Agabus
agabus_107.description: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine (Acts 11:27, 28). Many years afterwards he met Paul at Caesarea, and warned him of the bonds and affliction that awaited him at Jerusalem should he persist in going thither (Acts 21:10-12).

claudius_947.name: Claudius (4th Roman Emperor)
claudius_947.description: The fourth Roman emperor. He succeeded Caligula (A.D. 41). Though in general he treated the Jews, especially those in Asia and Egypt, with great indulgence, yet about the middle of his reign (A.D. 49) he banished them all from Rome (Acts 18:2). In this edict the Christians were included, as being, as was supposed, a…

herod_1506.name: Herod Agrippa I
herod_1506.description: Son of Aristobulus and Bernice, and grandson of Herod the Great. He was made tetrarch of the provinces formerly held by Lysanias II., and ultimately possessed the entire kingdom of his grandfather, Herod the Great, with the title of king. He put the apostle James the elder to death, and cast Peter into prison (Luke…

mary_1941.name: Mary (Mother of John Mark)
mary_1941.description: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church (Acts 4:37; 12:12). Her house in Jerusalem was the common meeting-place for the…

mark_1679.name: John Mark
mark_1679.description:
The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12, 25). Mark (Marcus, Col. 4:10, etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John. He is called John in Acts 13:5, 13, and Mark in 15:39, 2 Tim. 4:11, etc.

 He was the son of Mary, a woman apparently of some means and influence,…

rhoda_2439.name: Rhoda
rhoda_2439.description: A rose, the damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. She came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate (Acts 12:12-15).

blastus_518.name: Blastus
blastus_518.description: Chamberlain to king Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:20). Such persons generally had great influence with their masters.

simeon_2744.name: Simeon
simeon_2744.description: Surnamed Niger, i.e., “black,” perhaps from his dark complexion, a teacher of some distinction in the church of Antioch (Acts 13:1-3). It has been supposed that this was the Simon of Cyrene who bore Christ’s cross. Note the number of nationalities represented in the church at Antioch.

lucius_1833.name: Lucius
lucius_1833.description: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21). His name is Latin, but his birthplace seems to indicate that he was one of the Jews of Cyrene, in North Africa.

manaen_1926.name: Manaen
manaen_1926.description: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch. Nothing else is known of him beyond what is stated in Acts 13:1, where he is spoken of as having been brought up with (Gr. syntrophos; rendered in R.V. “foster brother” of) Herod, i.e., Herod Antipas, the tetrach, who, with his brother Archelaus, was educated at Rome.

elymas_403.name: Elymas
elymas_403.description: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus. He was miraculously struck with blindness (Acts 13:11).

sergius_2502.name: Sergius Paulus
sergius_2502.description:
A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13). He became a convert to Christianity under Paul, who visited this island on his first mission to the heathen.

 A remarkable memorial of this proconsul was recently (1887) discovered at Rome. On a boundary stone of…

judas_1759.name: Judas Barsabas
judas_1759.description: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32). He was a “prophet” and a “chief man among the brethren.”

silas_2740.name: Silas
silas_2740.description: Wood, a prominent member of the church at Jerusalem; also called Silvanus. He and Judas, surnamed Barsabas, were chosen by the church there to accompany Paul and Barnabas on their return to Antioch from the council of the apostles and elders (Acts 15:22), as bearers of the decree adopted by the council. He assisted…

timotheus_2863.name: Timotheus
timotheus_2863.description: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5). We know nothing of his father but that he was a Greek (Acts 16:1). He is first brought into notice at the time of Paul’s second…

jason_742.name: Jason
jason_742.description: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9). He was apparently one of the kinsmen of Paul (Rom. 16:21), and accompanied him from Thessalonica to Corinth.

dionysius_1013.name: Dionysius
dionysius_1013.description: The Areopagite, one of Paul’s converts at Athens (Acts 17:34).

damaris_972.name: Damaris
damaris_972.description: A heifer, an Athenian woman converted to Christianity under the preaching of Paul (Acts 17:34). Some have supposed that she may have been the wife of Dionysius the Areopagite.

aquila_279.name: Aquila
aquila_279.description: Eagle, a native of Pontus, by occupation a tent-maker, whom Paul met on his first visit to Corinth (Acts 18:2). Along with his wife Priscilla he had fled from Rome in consequence of a decree (A.D. 50) by Claudius commanding all Jews to leave the city. Paul sojourned with him at Corinth, and they wrought together at…

priscilla_2370.name: Priscilla
priscilla_2370.description: The wife of Aquila (Acts 18:2), who is never mentioned without her. Her name sometimes takes the precedence of his (Rom. 16:3; 2 Tim. 4:19). She took part with Aquila (q.v.) in insturcting Apollos (Acts 18:26).

justus_1766.name: Justus
justus_1766.description: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue (Acts 18:7).

crispus_961.name: Crispus
crispus_961.description: Curled, the chief of the synagogue at Corinth (Acts 18:8). He was converted and, with his family, baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

gallio_1275.name: Gallio
gallio_1275.description: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth (Acts 18:12). The word used here by Luke in describing the rank of Gallio shows his…

sosthenes_2772.name: Sosthenes
sosthenes_2772.description: Safe in strength, the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, who was seized and beaten by the mob in the presence of Gallio, the Roman governor, when he refused to proceed against Paul at the instigation of the Jews (Acts 18:12-17). The motives of this assault against Sosthenes are not recorded, nor is it mentioned…

apollos_276.name: Apollos
apollos_276.description: A Jew “born at Alexandria,” a man well versed in the Scriptures and eloquent (Acts 18:24; R.V., “learned”). He came to Ephesus (about A.D. 49), where he spake “boldly” in the synagogue (18:26), although he did not know as yet that Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah. Aquila and Priscilla instructed him more perfectly in…

tyrannus_2886.name: Tyrannus
tyrannus_2886.description: Prince, a Greek rhetorician, in whose “school” at Ephesus Paul disputed daily for the space of two years with those who came to him (Acts 19:9). Some have supposed that he was a Jew, and that his “school” was a private synagogue.

sceva_2480.name: Sceva
sceva_2480.description: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi. He had seven sons, who “took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus,” in imitation of Paul. They tried their method of exorcism on a fierce…

erastus_1213.name: Erastus
erastus_1213.description: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22). Corinth was his usual place of abode (2 Tim. 4:20); but probably he may have been the same as the preceding.

demetrius_1007.name: Demetrius
demetrius_1007.description: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana” (q.v.), Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess. This trade brought to him and his fellow-craftsmen “no small gain,” for these shrines found a ready sale among the countless thousands…

diana_1008.name: Diana
diana_1008.description: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications. Her most noted temple was that at Ephesus. It was built outside the city walls, and was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. “First and last it was the work of 220 years;…

gaius_1269.name: Gaius (of Macedonia)
gaius_1269.description: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into…

aristarchus_306.name: Aristarchus
aristarchus_306.description: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2). He was Paul’s “fellow-prisoner” at Rome (Col. 4:10; Philemon 1:24).

alexander_188.name: Alexander (Jew of Ephesus)
alexander_188.description: A Jew of Ephesus who took a prominent part in the uproar raised there by the preaching of Paul (Acts 19:33). The Jews put him forward to plead their cause before the mob. It was probably intended that he should show that he and the other Jews had no sympathy with Paul any more than the Ephesians had. It is possible…

sopater_2770.name: Sopater
sopater_2770.description: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

secundus_2482.name: Secundus
secundus_2482.description: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

gaius_1270.name: Gaius (of Derbe)
gaius_1270.description: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

tychicus_2885.name: Tychicus
tychicus_2885.description: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4). He is alluded to also in Col. 4:7, Titus 3:12, and 2 Tim. 4:12 as having been with Paul at Rome, whence he sent him to Ephesus,…

trophimus_2880.name: Trophimus
trophimus_2880.description: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment. (See  TEMPLE, HEROD’S.) In writing…

eutychus_1230.name: Eutychus
eutychus_1230.description: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.” The lattice-work of the window being open to admit the air, the lad fell out and down to the court below. Paul restored him to life again.…

mnason_2102.name: Mnason
mnason_2102.description: Reminding, or remembrancer, a Christian of Jerusalem with whom Paul lodged (Acts 21:16). He was apparently a native of Cyprus, like Barnabas (11:19, 20), and was well known to the Christians of Caesarea (4:36). He was an “old disciple” (R.V., “early disciple”), i.e., he had become a Christian in the beginning of the…

ananias_260.name: Ananias (High Priest)
ananias_260.description: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix (Acts 23:2, 5, 24). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth. Smarting under this unprovoked insult, Paul…

felix_1257.name: Felix
felix_1257.description:
Happy, the Roman procurator of Judea before whom Paul “reasoned” (Acts 24:25). He appears to have expected a bribe from Paul, and therefore had several interviews with him. The “worthy deeds” referred to in 24:2 was his clearing the country of banditti and impostors.

 At the end of a two years’ term, Porcius Festus…

claudius_948.name: Claudius Lysias
claudius_948.description: Claudius Lysias, a Greek who, having obtained by purchase the privilege of Roman citizenship, took the name of Claudius (Acts 21:31-40; 22:28; 23:26).

tertullus_2844.name: Tertullus
tertullus_2844.description: A modification of “Tertius;” a Roman advocate, whom the Jews employed to state their case against Paul in the presence of Felix (Acts 24:1-9). The charges he adduced against the apostle were, “First, that he created disturbances among the Romans throughout the empire, an offence against the Roman government (crimen…

drusilla_1024.name: Drusilla
drusilla_1024.description: Third and youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:1-4, 20-23). Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea, induced her to leave her husband, Azizus, the king of Emesa, and become his wife. She was present with Felix when Paul reasoned of “righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come” (Acts 24:24). She and her son…

portius_2367.name: Portius Festus
portius_2367.description: The successor of Felix (A.D. 60) as procurator of Judea (Acts 24:27). A few weeks after he had entered on his office the case of Paul, then a prisoner at Caesarea, was reported to him. The “next day,” after he had gone down to Caesarea, he heard Paul defend himself in the presence of Herod Agrippa II. and his sister…

agrippa_111.name: Agrippa
agrippa_111.description: Son of the foregoing, was born at Rome, A.D. 27. He was the brother of Bernice and Drusilla. The Emperor Claudius (A.D. 48) invested him with the office of superintendent of the Temple of Jerusalem, and made him governor (A.D. 50) of Chalcis. He was afterwards raised to the rank of king, and made governor over the…

bernice_482.name: Bernice
bernice_482.description: Bearer of victory, the eldest daughter of Agrippa I., the Herod Agrippa of Acts 12:20. After the early death of her first husband she was married to her uncle Herod, king of Chalcis. After his death (A.D. 40) she lived in incestuous connection with her brother Agrippa II. (Acts 25:13, 23; 26:30). They joined the…

julius_1763.name: Julius
julius_1763.description: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43). He entreated Paul “courteously,” showing in many ways a friendly regard for him.

publius_2374.name: Publius
publius_2374.description: “the chief man of the island” of Malta (Acts 28:7), who courteously entertained Paul and his shipwrecked companions for three days, till they found a more permanent place of residence; for they remained on the island for three months, till the stormy season had passed. The word here rendered “chief man” (protos) is…

phebe_2340.name: Phebe
phebe_2340.description: A “deaconess of the church at Cenchrea,” the port of Corinth. She was probably the bearer of Paul’s epistle to the Romans. Paul commended her to the Christians at Rome; “for she hath been,” says he, “a succourer of many, and of myself also” (Rom. 16:1, 2).

epaenetus_1194.name: Epaenetus
epaenetus_1194.description: Commendable, a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation (Rom. 16:5). He is spoken of as “the first fruits of Achaia” (R.V., “of Asia”, i.e., of proconsular Asia, which is probably the correct reading). As being the first convert in that region, he was peculiarly dear to the apostle. He calls him his “well…

mary_1942.name: Mary (of Rome)
mary_1942.description: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness (Rom. 16:6).

andronicus_265.name: Andronicus
andronicus_265.description: Man-conquering, a Jewish Christian, the kinsman and fellowprisoner of Paul (Rom. 16:7); “of note among the apostles.”

junia_1764.name: Junia
junia_1764.description: (Rom. 16:7), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

amplias_241.name: Amplias
amplias_241.description: A Roman Christian saluted by Paul (Rom. 16:8).

stachys_2774.name: Stachys
stachys_2774.description: Spike; an ear of corn, a convert at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:9).

apelles_273.name: Apelles
apelles_273.description: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:10), and styles “approved in Christ.”

herodion_1508.name: Herodion
herodion_1508.description: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes and calls his “kinsman” (Rom. 16:11).

narcissus_2151.name: Narcissus
narcissus_2151.description: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:11). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius. This is, however, quite uncertain.

persis_2317.name: Persis
persis_2317.description: A female Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:12). She is spoken of as “beloved,” and as having “laboured much in the Lord.”

phlegon_2352.name: Phlegon
phlegon_2352.description: Burning, a Roman Christian to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

patrobas_2289.name: Patrobas
patrobas_2289.description: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

julia_1762.name: Julia
julia_1762.description: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations (Rom. 16:15), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

olympas_2241.name: Olympas
olympas_2241.description: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:15).

gaius_1271.name: Gaius
gaius_1271.description: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into…

quartus_2378.name: Quartus
quartus_2378.description: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

chloe_943.name: Chloe
chloe_943.description: Verdure, a female Christian (1 Cor. 1:11), some of whose household had informed Paul of the divided state of the Corinthian church. Nothing is known of her.

stephanas_2801.name: Stephanas
